c2326575.oQueMuda: States that everyone has the right to digital inclusion and that the government must have policies to expand internet access, as set by law. On its own, it does not create programs, funding or penalties.
c2326575.quemAfeta: People without internet access and governments.
c2326575.porQueImporta: The Brazilian Internet Bill of Rights already treats access as essential; the change brings this right into the Constitution and calls for public policies.

c464909.titulo: Creates a single national career for public doctors
c464909.oQueMuda: Sets guidelines for a national career for doctors in public service.
c464909.quemAfeta: Doctors and patients of the public health system (SUS).
c464909.porQueImporta: A national career could bring doctors to towns that cannot hire them today, but would be costly for the federal government and change who hires doctors, today mostly city governments.

c356309.titulo: Changes rules for creating or merging municipalities
c356309.oQueMuda: Creating, merging or splitting municipalities would have to preserve historical and cultural unity and happen up to 12 months before elections.
c356309.quemAfeta: Residents of areas seeking to become a municipality.
c356309.porQueImporta: It would make it easier to create new towns, which could bring government closer to remote districts, but each new city government and council has costs and splits FPM money among more towns.

c2209776.titulo: Gives health insurance to former Sucam workers exposed to DDT
c2209776.oQueMuda: Former employees who handled the pesticide DDT would be entitled to health insurance.
c2209776.quemAfeta: Former employees of the old Sucam agency.
c2209776.porQueImporta: Former employees who fell ill after handling DDT would get health care paid by the federal government, a new expense limited to this group.

s8563075.titulo: Adds inclusive education to the principles of education
s8563075.oQueMuda: Adds to the principles of education a guarantee of inclusive teaching at all levels, considering each student's needs. On its own, it does not create programs, funding or penalties.
s8563075.quemAfeta: Students with disabilities or specific needs, schools and school systems.
s8563075.porQueImporta: The Constitution already provides specialized support for students with disabilities, preferably in regular schools; the change extends the principle to all levels.

c1618422.titulo: Restores income tax exemption for retirees over 65
c1618422.oQueMuda: It brings back an old rule that exempted from income tax, within legal limits, pensions of people over 65 who live only on that income.
c1618422.porQueImporta: Retirees over 65 would pay less tax, and the federal government and state and municipal funds, which get part of income tax, would collect less.

c2140425.oQueMuda: Public consultations would take place on election day.
c2140425.porQueImporta: Referendums would become cheaper and could be held more often, but would compete with the election for voters' attention.

c2084889.titulo: Requires Congress's approval for heads of state-owned companies
c2084889.oQueMuda: Presidents and directors of federal companies would have to be approved by Congress.
c2084889.quemAfeta: State-owned companies such as Petrobras and public banks.
c2084889.porQueImporta: Heads of state companies would need congressional approval, increasing control over appointments but possibly turning these posts into bargaining chips.

c460138.titulo: Creates a fund to maintain the public safety system
c460138.oQueMuda: Creates a fund for maintaining and developing public safety.
c460138.porQueImporta: Public security would have earmarked money, giving police stable funding but reducing governments' room to decide where to spend.

c540302.titulo: Creates a national system and minimum spending on public safety
c540302.oQueMuda: Federal and state governments would have to spend minimum percentages on public safety.
c540302.porQueImporta: Public security would have mandatory minimum spending, like health and education; this guarantees funding for police but reduces room for other budget areas.

c568527.titulo: Requires recorded votes on provisional measures
c568527.oQueMuda: Each legislator would have to record their vote on provisional measures (executive decrees).
c568527.porQueImporta: Voters could see how each lawmaker voted on each provisional measure; votes would be slower than symbolic (voice) votes.

s1399166.titulo: Lets states make laws protecting older people
s1399166.oQueMuda: Federal and state governments would share the power to make laws protecting older people.
s1399166.porQueImporta: States could create their own laws protecting older people, allowing them to go beyond national rules but possibly creating different rules between states.

s8834618.oQueMuda: The word 'agrotóxicos' would be replaced by 'pesticidas' in the constitutional text.
s8834618.porQueImporta: Replacing 'agrotóxico' (agro-toxic) with 'pesticide' does not change usage rules, but removes from the Constitution a word that highlights the toxic risk of these products, as the farm sector advocates.

s8834813.titulo: Bans freezing science and technology fund money
s8834813.oQueMuda: Spending from the National Science and Technology Development Fund (FNDCT) could not be frozen by the government.
s8834813.porQueImporta: Scientific research money could not be frozen in spending cuts, giving projects predictability but forcing the government to cut more elsewhere when money is short.

s8255099.oQueMuda: The President, governors and mayors could not be reelected and would serve five-year terms.
s8255099.quemAfeta: Voters and heads of the executive branch.
s8255099.porQueImporta: Each leader would have a single five-year term; this reduces use of government resources for re-election but prevents voters from keeping leaders they approve of.

s8794275.titulo: Cuts social security contributions for inland cities
s8794275.oQueMuda: Inland city governments would pay lower contributions on their payroll.
s8794275.quemAfeta: Inland city governments and social security.
s8794275.porQueImporta: Inland city governments would pay less into social security and have more money for other spending; INSS would collect less, increasing its deficit.

c489897.titulo: Gives union confederations part of union dues
c489897.oQueMuda: National union confederations would receive part of union dues.
c489897.porQueImporta: Union federations would have their own source of money; today the union contribution is no longer mandatory by law, so the effect depends on it being collected again.

s1395667.titulo: Adds basic sanitation to the social rights
s1395667.oQueMuda: Adds basic sanitation to the Constitution's list of social rights (article 6). On its own, it does not create programs, funding or penalties.
s1395667.quemAfeta: People without clean water or sewage, and governments.
s1395667.porQueImporta: It would give a constitutional basis for demanding clean water and sewage; today sanitation appears only as a government task, not as a right.

s8309893.titulo: Creates a minimum salary for physical and occupational therapists
s8309893.oQueMuda: Establishes a national minimum salary for these professions.
s8309893.quemAfeta: Physical therapists, occupational therapists and employers.
s8309893.porQueImporta: It would raise the minimum pay of these professions, but also costs for clinics, hospitals and health plans, which may pass them on to patients.

s7849279.titulo: Creates a fund to repair environmental damage from mining and oil
s7849279.oQueMuda: 1% of federal revenue from oil, gas and minerals would go to preventing and repairing environmental damage.
s7849279.porQueImporta: Money would be set aside to prevent and repair environmental disasters, like those in Mariana and Brumadinho, but the share of oil and mining revenue available for other spending would shrink.

c2499794.titulo: Creates a minimum salary for police and firefighters
c2499794.oQueMuda: Civil police, military police and firefighters would have a national minimum salary.
c2499794.quemAfeta: Police officers, firefighters and state governments.
c2499794.porQueImporta: It would raise police and firefighter pay in many states, but state governments, which already spend heavily on staff, would have to find the money.

c2435133.titulo: Creates a special regime to rebuild Rio Grande do Sul
c2435133.oQueMuda: Relaxes fiscal and procurement rules to deal with the flood disaster and support affected families.
c2435133.quemAfeta: Residents and the government of Rio Grande do Sul.
c2435133.porQueImporta: It would allow faster spending and hiring for rebuilding Rio Grande do Sul, but with fewer controls, increasing the risk of poorly managed spending.

c2231888.titulo: Guarantees income for families in poverty
c2231888.oQueMuda: Adds to the Constitution an anti-poverty policy with cash transfers to poor families.
c2231888.quemAfeta: Families in poverty and extreme poverty.
c2231888.porQueImporta: A cash-transfer program would be guaranteed in the Constitution, protected from changes in government, creating a permanent item in the budget.

s8796486.titulo: Allows a regional bonus for admission to public higher education
s8796486.oQueMuda: Public institutions could give a bonus to applicants from poorer regions.
s8796486.porQueImporta: Candidates from poorer regions would have better chances at public universities, which may reduce regional inequality but decreases places for candidates from elsewhere.

c1738895.titulo: Sets rules and deadlines for creating municipalities
c1738895.oQueMuda: Sets procedures and timing for creating, merging or splitting municipalities.
c1738895.quemAfeta: Residents of districts and state governments.
c1738895.porQueImporta: It would unblock the creation of new towns, which could serve remote districts, but each new city government has costs and splits FPM among more municipalities.

c598858.titulo: Adds maritime policing to military police duties
c598858.oQueMuda: Military police would also patrol coastal waters.
c598858.porQueImporta: Military police could patrol the sea, expanding coastal surveillance but possibly overlapping with the Navy and Federal Police.

c263327.oQueMuda: Changes rules on union registration, collective bargaining and worker representation.
c263327.porQueImporta: It would change how unions are formed and negotiate, affecting workers' bargaining power and the power of existing unions.

c277153.titulo: Ends the single-union rule and creates a bargaining fee
c277153.oQueMuda: Allows more than one union per category, creates a collective bargaining fee and workplace representation.
c277153.porQueImporta: More than one union per profession increases workers' freedom of choice but may split and weaken representation; the new contribution would be charged per bargaining agreement.

c292210.titulo: Renames collective labor disputes as 'normative actions'
c292210.oQueMuda: Collective cases in the Labor Courts would be called normative actions, filed by unions.
c292210.porQueImporta: It would change how strikes and collective disputes reach the Labor Courts, affecting the power of unions and companies in these disputes.

c489621.titulo: Gives states back the power to create municipalities
c489621.oQueMuda: States could again make laws on creating, merging and splitting municipalities.
c489621.quemAfeta: Residents of districts seeking independence and state governments.
c489621.porQueImporta: States could create new towns without waiting for the federal law; this serves districts wanting independence but tends to multiply city governments and councils, with more costs and FPM split among more towns.

c502631.titulo: Changes rules for creating or merging municipalities
c502631.oQueMuda: Creating, merging or splitting municipalities would have to preserve historical and cultural unity and happen up to 12 months before elections.
c502631.quemAfeta: Residents of areas seeking to become a municipality.
c502631.porQueImporta: It would make it easier to create new towns, which could bring government closer to remote districts, but each new city government and council has costs and splits FPM money among more towns.

c2162097.titulo: Bars judges from cases tied to whoever appointed them
c2162097.oQueMuda: Judges could not take part in cases involving the president or governor who appointed them.
c2162097.quemAfeta: Judges and justices appointed by the executive.
c2162097.porQueImporta: Judges could not rule on cases involving the president or governor who appointed them, reducing conflicts of interest but possibly leaving courts with few justices able to hear these cases.

c2233327.titulo: Makes it easier to change municipal borders
c2233327.oQueMuda: Sets rules to split, merge or redraw municipal borders without creating new cities.
c2233327.quemAfeta: Residents of border areas and city governments.
c2233327.porQueImporta: It would make it easier to settle territorial disputes between towns, affecting who collects taxes and provides services in these areas.

s8809676.titulo: Sends part of the education payroll contribution to public daycare
s8809676.oQueMuda: States and cities would have to use a share of the education payroll contribution to open and run daycare centers.
s8809676.quemAfeta: Young children, families and city governments.
s8809676.porQueImporta: More money would have to go to daycare, which tends to open places for young children, but less salário-educação money would be left for other school levels.

s8540294.titulo: Changes rules for active-duty military running for office
s8540294.oQueMuda: Members of the armed forces who want to run would have to move to the reserve when registering as candidates.
s8540294.porQueImporta: Active-duty military personnel would have to leave active service to run, keeping barracks away from politics but making military candidacies harder.

c2487390.titulo: Expands audit court oversight of multinational companies with federal stakes
c2487390.oQueMuda: Congress and the federal audit court (TCU) could audit supranational companies in which the federal government has a stake.
c2487390.porQueImporta: The Federal Audit Court could audit companies such as Itaipu, expanding control over public money but requiring agreement with the other partner country.

s8808203.titulo: Requires anyone summoned to appear before inquiry committees
s8808203.oQueMuda: Citizens and officials summoned by parliamentary inquiry committees would have to appear.
s8808203.quemAfeta: People summoned by parliamentary inquiry committees.
s8808203.porQueImporta: Inquiry committees could compel anyone to appear, strengthening congressional investigations but possibly clashing with the right not to incriminate oneself.

c348335.titulo: Ties pension increases to the minimum wage
c348335.oQueMuda: Social security benefits would get the same increase as the minimum wage, and the cap would rise to ten minimum wages.
c348335.quemAfeta: Retirees and pensioners of the national social security system (INSS).
c348335.porQueImporta: INSS retirees would get bigger raises, but social security spending, already the largest federal expense, would rise sharply.

c1738778.titulo: Exempts police hazard bonuses from taxes
c1738778.oQueMuda: Hazard and life-risk bonuses paid to police would not be taxed.
c1738778.porQueImporta: Police officers would take home more, and the federal and state governments would collect less income tax; it sets a precedent for other professions to seek exemptions.

c2018276.titulo: Sets priority and urgency criteria in health care
c2018276.oQueMuda: Keeps the universal right to health but sets criteria to define priorities and emergencies.
c2018276.quemAfeta: Patients of the public health system (SUS).
c2018276.porQueImporta: Priority criteria could organize public health queues, but also open room to deny or delay treatments that today are obtained through the courts.

c2189436.titulo: Lists academic freedom among the fundamental rights
c2189436.oQueMuda: Adds 'teaching' (academic freedom) to the right to free intellectual, artistic and scientific expression. On its own, it does not create programs, funding or penalties.
c2189436.porQueImporta: The Constitution already guarantees freedom to teach and research among the principles of education; the change repeats this guarantee in the list of fundamental rights.

c2307037.titulo: Adds basic income to the social rights
c2307037.oQueMuda: States that every Brazilian with insufficient income has the right to a basic income, with amount and rules set by law. On its own, it does not create the benefit: a law is needed.
c2307037.quemAfeta: Low-income people and the federal government.
c2307037.porQueImporta: A similar rule, on family basic income, was already added to the Constitution in 2021 (Amendment 114); this proposal was filed before that.

c1738617.titulo: Ends the stay-on bonus for civil servants
c1738617.oQueMuda: Civil servants who can already retire but keep working would stop receiving this bonus.
c1738617.porQueImporta: The government would save on the bonus, but experienced civil servants may retire earlier, increasing pension spending and requiring new hires.

c2057623.titulo: Changes the share of funds sent to the BNDES
c2057623.oQueMuda: Changes the share of PIS/PASEP money passed to the national development bank (BNDES) for loans.
c2057623.quemAfeta: The BNDES and companies that borrow from it.
c2057623.porQueImporta: It would change how much PIS/PASEP money goes to BNDES to lend to companies, affecting cheap credit for investment and funds for unemployment insurance.

c2233640.titulo: Allows city fire brigades with volunteers
c2233640.oQueMuda: Cities could create fire brigades through agreements with volunteer firefighters.
c2233640.porQueImporta: Towns without a fire station would get emergency response, but from volunteers, who may have less training and equipment than military firefighters.

c2344523.titulo: Cuts property tax (IPTU) on land with native vegetation
c2344523.oQueMuda: The urban property tax would have environmental criteria, and areas with native vegetation would be tax-free.
c2344523.quemAfeta: Owners of urban property with preserved woodland and city governments.
c2344523.porQueImporta: Owners of land with native vegetation would pay less property tax, likely encouraging preservation of green areas but reducing city revenue.

c2220682.titulo: Bans extra perks on top public salaries
c2220682.oQueMuda: Officials earning more than a quarter of a Supreme Court justice's salary could not receive add-ons without express provision.
c2220682.quemAfeta: Civil servants and officials with high salaries.
c2220682.porQueImporta: It would cut extra payments to those already earning high public salaries, reducing spending and pay gaps; affected careers would lose part of their current income.

c458500.titulo: Merges civil and military police and demilitarizes firefighters
c458500.oQueMuda: Creates a single state police force replacing civil and military police and makes firefighters civilian.
c458500.quemAfeta: Police officers, firefighters and municipal guards.
c458500.porQueImporta: A single police force could reduce disputes and duplicated costs between military and civil police, but would require a huge reorganization of careers and face strong resistance from the forces.

c2165018.titulo: Bans recent party membership for electoral court members
c2165018.oQueMuda: People serving in the electoral courts could not have been party members in the previous two years.
c2165018.quemAfeta: Judges and lawyers who sit on electoral courts.
c2165018.porQueImporta: People recently affiliated with a party could not judge elections, reducing the risk of bias but shrinking the pool of lawyers who can sit on these courts.

c2221671.oQueMuda: Postal services could be run by private companies under authorization or concession.
c2221671.quemAfeta: The postal service (Correios), its employees and users.
c2221671.porQueImporta: Private companies could deliver mail, which could bring competition and efficiency, but there is a risk of worse service or higher prices in small towns, where delivery loses money.

c2139404.titulo: Caps interest payments on the public debt
c2139404.oQueMuda: Sets a limit on what the federal government spends on interest and debt charges.
c2139404.quemAfeta: The federal government and the country's creditors.
c2139404.porQueImporta: Capping interest payments would free money for other areas, but could worry creditors, make new government borrowing more expensive and affect confidence in the economy.

c2181063.titulo: Reduces the number of senators and deputies
c2181063.oQueMuda: Reduces the number of senators, federal deputies and state deputies.
c2181063.porQueImporta: Fewer lawmakers would reduce legislative costs, but each would represent more voters, and smaller states and groups could lose their voice.

c110958.titulo: Establishes full freedom of association for unions
c110958.oQueMuda: Changes union organization rules, allowing more freedom to create organizations.
c110958.porQueImporta: Workers would have more freedom to create unions, increasing choice but possibly splitting and weakening representation in negotiations with companies.

c423901.titulo: Gives the Labor Courts power to try labor crimes
c423901.oQueMuda: Crimes such as slave labor and crimes against labor organization would be tried by the Labor Courts.
c423901.quemAfeta: Workers, employers and the federal courts.
c423901.porQueImporta: Crimes such as slave labor would be tried by judges specialized in labor relations, which could speed up and improve these cases but shifts a power that today belongs to federal courts.

c2487818.titulo: Allows summoning the Central Bank president
c2487818.oQueMuda: The Central Bank president could be summoned by the Chamber, the Senate or their committees.
c2487818.porQueImporta: Congress could compel the Central Bank president to explain himself, increasing oversight but also political pressure on interest-rate policy.

c2487249.titulo: Guarantees lawyers the right to argue in person or online
c2487249.oQueMuda: Strengthens the lawyer's role and guarantees the right to speak at hearings, in person or online.
c2487249.porQueImporta: Lawyers would be guaranteed the right to speak at hearings, strengthening the defense but possibly slowing down court schedules.

s8664217.titulo: Makes the Mato Grosso do Sul Pantanal national heritage
s8664217.oQueMuda: The Pantanal of Mato Grosso do Sul would be added to the national heritage areas.
s8664217.quemAfeta: Residents and producers in the Pantanal.
s8664217.porQueImporta: The Pantanal in Mato Grosso do Sul would have its use conditioned on preservation, like the Amazon, strengthening environmental protection and possibly limiting economic activity in the region.

s8771508.titulo: Lowers the new tax on water and sewage
s8771508.oQueMuda: Changes the tax reform to reduce IBS and CBS rates on water and sewage services.
s8771508.porQueImporta: Water and sewage bills would carry less tax, but the lost revenue tends to be offset by a higher rate on other goods and services.

s7817905.oQueMuda: Children would be a social security priority, with a monthly benefit for those living in poverty.
s7817905.porQueImporta: Poor children would have a monthly benefit guaranteed in the Constitution, likely reducing child poverty but creating a permanent cost for social security.

s8403373.titulo: Exempts rare disease medicines from taxes
s8403373.oQueMuda: Medicines to treat rare diseases would be tax-free.
s8403373.quemAfeta: Patients with rare diseases and their families.
s8403373.porQueImporta: Medicines for rare diseases, usually very expensive, could become cheaper for patients and for the public health system, with a small loss of revenue.

s8477226.titulo: Requires a National Food Security Plan
s8477226.oQueMuda: The Constitution would require a national plan against hunger and for good nutrition.
s8477226.porQueImporta: Governments would need a plan against hunger, with targets, giving continuity to these policies, but the Constitution does not say where the money would come from.

s8656750.titulo: Creates the National Climate Emergency Fund
s8656750.oQueMuda: Creates a fund to guarantee money for floods, droughts and other climate disasters.
s8656750.porQueImporta: Money would be set aside to respond to floods and droughts, speeding up aid but requiring funds that today go to other areas.

s8542259.titulo: Makes possession of any amount of drugs a crime
s8542259.oQueMuda: The Constitution would require that unauthorized possession and carrying of drugs be a crime in any amount, distinguishing users from traffickers and providing alternatives to prison and treatment for users.
s8542259.quemAfeta: Drug users and the justice system.
s8542259.porQueImporta: Anyone caught with any amount of drugs would still face criminal charges, even after the Supreme Court's 2024 ruling on marijuana; users would get alternative sentences, but with a criminal record.

c2075449.titulo: Extends maternity leave for premature births
c2075449.oQueMuda: Time the premature baby spends in hospital would not be deducted from maternity leave.
c2075449.quemAfeta: Mothers of premature babies and employers.
c2075449.porQueImporta: Mothers of premature babies would have more time at home with the baby, and INSS would pay more weeks of leave.

s8792757.titulo: Cuts the workweek to 40 hours and 5 days
s8792757.oQueMuda: The maximum would drop from 44 to 40 hours, over up to 5 days and 8 hours a day, with days off preferably on weekends.
s8792757.porQueImporta: People who work more than 40 hours or six days a week today would have more free time with no pay cut, which the text guarantees. The wage cost per hour would rise for companies; they would likely have to reorganize shifts, hire more, pay overtime or invest in productivity, and economists disagree on which effect would weigh most.

c2483164.oQueMuda: The president would appoint a prime minister to govern, and deputies would be elected by a mixed district system.
c2483164.porQueImporta: The president would share power with a prime minister who depends on Congress, and deputies would be partly elected by district; this may make it easier to change governments in a crisis, but changes who holds governing power.

c2229938.titulo: Speeds up the end of cases by limiting appeals
c2229938.oQueMuda: Appeals to the Supreme Court and the Superior Court of Justice would become review actions, and second-instance rulings would be final.
c2229938.quemAfeta: Defendants, parties to cases and higher courts.
c2229938.porQueImporta: People convicted on appeal would start serving sentences earlier, likely speeding up punishment but reducing the chance to correct errors in higher courts.

s1395980.titulo: Allows Congress to summon heads of state companies and agencies
s1395980.oQueMuda: The Chamber, the Senate and committees could summon heads of federal indirect administration bodies.
s1395980.quemAfeta: Heads of state-owned companies, agencies and authorities.
s1395980.porQueImporta: Congress could summon more officials to explain themselves, expanding oversight of the government and also political pressure on technical bodies.

c14493.titulo: Lowers the age of criminal responsibility to 16
c14493.oQueMuda: Young people from 16 would be tried as adults.
c14493.quemAfeta: Teenagers aged 16 and 17 and the justice system.
c14493.porQueImporta: More teenagers would go into the adult prison system, which is already overcrowded and where gangs recruit inmates; punishment would be harsher and prison costs would rise.

c516111.titulo: Changes the process for provisional measures
c516111.oQueMuda: Changes deadlines and review steps for provisional measures (executive decrees) and bans reissuing them.
c516111.porQueImporta: The president would have less room to govern by provisional measures, giving Congress more power but possibly delaying quick government responses.

c786713.titulo: Unifies disability retirement rules for civil servants
c786713.oQueMuda: Sets the same rule for disability retirement and a transition for those who joined the civil service by 2003.
c786713.porQueImporta: Civil servants retired for disability could receive higher amounts, increasing public pension spending.

c946494.oQueMuda: The government would have to carry out deputies' and senators' individual budget amendments.
c946494.quemAfeta: Legislators, cities and the federal government.
c946494.porQueImporta: Already in force: the government must pay individual budget amendments, giving lawmakers control over part of the budget and reducing the government's room to set priorities.

c1526944.titulo: Creates a special regime to pay overdue court debts
c1526944.oQueMuda: Sets rules for paying governments' court-ordered debts and a special regime for overdue cases.
c1526944.quemAfeta: People and companies that won lawsuits against governments.
c1526944.porQueImporta: Governments would get more time to pay court-ordered debts, easing their finances, but people who won lawsuits against them would wait longer to be paid.

c2209349.titulo: Makes state caucus budget amendments mandatory
c2209349.oQueMuda: The government would have to carry out the collective budget amendments of state caucuses.
c2209349.quemAfeta: Legislators, states and the federal government.
c2209349.porQueImporta: Already in force: the government must pay state caucus amendments, giving lawmakers control over another part of the budget and reducing the government's room.

c606656.titulo: Adds human rights to the principles of the economy
c606656.oQueMuda: Adds 'respect for human rights' to the principles of the economy and describes the system as 'humanist capitalism'. On its own, it does not create programs, funding or penalties.
c606656.quemAfeta: Companies, governments and those who make economic laws.
c606656.porQueImporta: It would serve as guidance for interpreting economic laws and policies.

s8735431.titulo: Changes rules for inquiries opened by courts
s8735431.oQueMuda: Sets when courts can open inquiries into crimes at their premises or against their members.
s8735431.quemAfeta: Courts, especially the Supreme Court, and people under investigation.
s8735431.porQueImporta: It would limit investigations opened by the Supreme Court itself, such as the fake news inquiry, reducing the court's power to investigate attacks against it but also criticism that it investigates and judges at the same time.

s8735562.titulo: Creates disciplinary complaints against Supreme Court justices
s8735562.oQueMuda: Supreme Court justices could face disciplinary complaints for conduct outside impeachable offenses.
s8735562.porQueImporta: Supreme Court justices could face disciplinary punishment, increasing control over their conduct but possibly being used to pressure the court over its rulings.

s8739428.titulo: Changes the makeup of the Electoral Court and removes Supreme Court justices from it
s8739428.oQueMuda: The Superior Electoral Court (TSE) would have 7 members with 2-year terms: 2 justices of the Superior Court of Justice (STJ), 1 lawyer nominated by the Bar Association and appointed by the president, 2 chosen by the Chamber and 2 by the Senate.
s8739428.quemAfeta: The Electoral Court, the Supreme Court, Congress and voters.
s8739428.porQueImporta: The Chamber and Senate would choose 4 of the 7 judges of the court that rules on elections and can remove candidates, increasing politicians' influence over who judges them.

s8749240.titulo: Changes rules for approving and paying budget amendments
s8749240.oQueMuda: Creates criteria for approving and paying legislators' amendments to budget laws.
s8749240.porQueImporta: It would change the transparency and control of budget amendments, which today total tens of billions of reais a year and are the target of investigations into misuse.

s8772231.titulo: Creates technical criteria for choosing federal audit court ministers
s8772231.oQueMuda: Requires technical criteria and bans appointing recent politicians and relatives to the Federal Court of Accounts (TCU).
s8772231.porQueImporta: Recent politicians and relatives could not be appointed to the Federal Audit Court, reducing political appointments but also the influence of Congress and the president over the court.

s8776422.titulo: Creates gender parity in judges' promotions
s8776422.oQueMuda: Guarantees quotas for women in promoting judges to appeals courts.
s8776422.porQueImporta: More women judges would reach appellate courts, where they are a minority today; male judges would have fewer promotion slots for some time.

s8780865.titulo: Removes from jury trial killings attributed to gangs, militias and criminal groups
s8780865.oQueMuda: Intentional crimes against life, such as homicide, committed by members of a criminal association, militia or criminal organization would be decided by a single judge rather than a jury of citizens.
s8780865.quemAfeta: Defendants accused of these crimes, victims and their families, jurors and criminal judges.
s8780865.porQueImporta: Jury trial is a constitutional guarantee for crimes against life. Under the law, a 'criminal association' can be a group of just three people, so the change could reach many cases beyond large gangs; the authors say the goal is to prevent threats against jurors.

c2428346.titulo: Adds care to the social rights
c2428346.oQueMuda: Adds 'care' (for older people, children, people with disabilities and other dependents) to the list of social rights. On its own, it does not create programs, funding or penalties.
c2428346.quemAfeta: People who need care, their caregivers and governments.
c2428346.porQueImporta: A National Care Policy was already created by law in 2024; the change would give this right a basis in the Constitution.

c348719.titulo: Tax reform with a financial transactions tax
c348719.oQueMuda: Creates selective taxes, a financial transactions tax of up to 0.76%, and ends the CSLL and the large fortunes tax.
c348719.quemAfeta: All taxpayers, states and the federal government.
c348719.porQueImporta: It would change the entire tax structure, with a tax on financial transactions similar to the old CPMF, which is easy to collect but weighs on everyone and makes transactions more expensive.

c355705.titulo: Increases the share of vehicle tax (IPVA) kept by cities
c355705.oQueMuda: Cities would get a bigger share of the IPVA from vehicles registered in their territory.
c355705.porQueImporta: City governments would keep more IPVA and states less, changing who pays for services such as roads and security.

c357691.oQueMuda: No taxes could be created on producing and selling essential foods.
c357691.porQueImporta: Basic foods would be tax-free, which could make the basic food basket cheaper, especially for the poorest, but reduces state and federal revenue.

c360826.titulo: Cuts the IPI tax on products made from recycled material
c360826.oQueMuda: Manufactured goods using recycled material would pay less IPI.
c360826.porQueImporta: Products with recycled materials would become cheaper, likely encouraging recycling, with a loss of IPI revenue, which is also shared with states and municipalities.

c370136.titulo: Exempts people with disabilities from income and property taxes
c370136.oQueMuda: People with disabilities would not pay taxes on their income or on buying and selling goods for their own use.
c370136.porQueImporta: People with disabilities would have higher income by not paying tax, regardless of whether they are rich or poor, and governments would collect less.

c370580.titulo: Rewards states and cities with conservation areas
c370580.oQueMuda: Up to 0.5% of participation fund transfers would go to states and cities with environmental conservation areas.
c370580.quemAfeta: States and cities with protected areas.
c370580.porQueImporta: States and cities with protected areas would receive more, creating an incentive to preserve, but would take part of the transfers from other cities and states.

c370778.titulo: Creates a rural support fund from federal transfers
c370778.oQueMuda: 3% of federal revenue sent to cities would go to a special fund supporting agriculture.
c370778.porQueImporta: Farming would have guaranteed money, but the earmarked share would come out of transfers to city governments, reducing their freedom to decide where to spend.

c383286.titulo: Defines where money from new federal taxes goes
c383286.oQueMuda: Sets where the revenue from any new or increased federal tax would go.
c383286.porQueImporta: New federal taxes would have a set destination, giving transparency but reducing the government's freedom to use the money where it is most needed.

c384058.titulo: Changes compensation to states for exports
c384058.oQueMuda: Changes the compensation the federal government pays states for losses from tax exemptions on exports.
c384058.porQueImporta: It would change how much the federal government pays exporting states for tax exemptions on exports, affecting the finances of states such as Minas Gerais, Pará and Mato Grosso.

c384059.titulo: Bans social contributions on government revenue
c384059.oQueMuda: The federal government, states, the Federal District, municipalities and public agencies would no longer pay social contributions on revenue, such as PIS/Pasep.
c384059.quemAfeta: All levels of government and the social security system, which receives these contributions.
c384059.porQueImporta: States and municipalities would stop paying these contributions and have more money, but social security, which pays pensions and health care, would lose revenue.

c384060.titulo: Splits sales tax on online purchases between states
c384060.oQueMuda: In online sales between states, part of the ICMS would go to the buyer's state.
c384060.porQueImporta: States whose residents buy most online would collect more, and states where large online retailers are based would collect less; a similar rule has been in the Constitution since 2015.

c384544.titulo: Cuts taxes on machinery and equipment
c384544.oQueMuda: Capital goods, such as industrial machines, would be exempt from IPI and ICMS.
c384544.porQueImporta: Machinery would become cheaper, which could encourage investment and production, with lost revenue for the federal government, states and municipalities.

c384954.titulo: Creates a federal VAT by merging contributions
c384954.oQueMuda: Combines Cofins, PIS and Cide into a value-added tax and folds the CSLL into corporate income tax.
c384954.porQueImporta: Merging federal taxes into one would simplify things for companies but change how much each sector pays; the 2023 tax reform already took a similar path.

c389981.oQueMuda: Creates a minimum tax on financial transactions and transfers.
c389981.quemAfeta: Everyone who moves money through banks.
c389981.porQueImporta: A tax on financial transactions raises a lot and is hard to evade, but is charged to everyone, including the poorest, and makes every bank transaction more expensive.

c391353.oQueMuda: Employers would stop paying social contributions on salaries.
c391353.porQueImporta: Hiring would become cheaper, which could encourage formal jobs, but social security would lose its main source of funding, which would have to be replaced by another tax.

c440021.titulo: Creates a single tax on goods and services
c440021.oQueMuda: Creates a non-cumulative tax on transactions with goods or services, including imports.
c440021.porQueImporta: A single consumption tax would simplify collection but change how much each sector and state collects; the 2023 tax reform already adopted a similar model.

c604132.titulo: Creates a welfare benefit for crime victims
c604132.oQueMuda: Crime victims would be entitled to a social assistance benefit.
c604132.porQueImporta: Crime victims would gain support that does not exist today, creating a new cost for social assistance.

c1229857.titulo: Ends the benefit for prisoners' families
c1229857.oQueMuda: The benefit paid to prisoners' dependents would be removed from social security.
c1229857.porQueImporta: Low-income prisoners' families, usually with young children, would lose this income; social security would save on the benefit.

c1712462.titulo: Gives a monthly benefit to dependents of homicide victims
c1712462.oQueMuda: Dependents of people who were murdered would receive one minimum wage a month.
c1712462.porQueImporta: Families of homicide victims would have a monthly income, creating a new and permanent cost for social assistance.

c2113815.titulo: Swaps the prisoners' family benefit for one for victims' families
c2113815.oQueMuda: Ends the benefit for prisoners' families and gives one minimum wage a month to dependents of homicide victims.
c2113815.quemAfeta: Families of prisoners and of homicide victims.
c2113815.porQueImporta: Low-income prisoners' families would lose the benefit and families of homicide victims would start receiving one; the final cost depends on how many people fall in each group.

c2140762.titulo: Ties the prisoners' family benefit to the prisoner working
c2140762.oQueMuda: The benefit for dependents would only be paid if the convicted prisoner works.
c2140762.porQueImporta: Many prisoners' families would lose the benefit, because there are few jobs available in prisons; social security would save money.

c2474283.oQueMuda: Changes rules on super-salaries, the BPC disability and elderly benefit, the Fundeb education fund and the wage bonus, and extends the DRU to 2032.
c2474283.quemAfeta: Civil servants, BPC and wage bonus recipients, and basic education.
c2474283.porQueImporta: Already in force: it slowed spending growth on the wage bonus, BPC and very high public salaries, helping public finances but reducing benefits for some recipients.

c14638.titulo: Cuts the workweek from 44 to 30 hours
c14638.oQueMuda: The workweek would drop one hour a year down to 30 hours, with agreements allowing up to 40.
c14638.porQueImporta: People who work more than 30 hours would have much more free time without losing pay. For those going from 44 to 30 hours, the wage cost per hour rises about 47%; companies would likely have to reorganize shifts, hire more, pay overtime or invest in productivity, and economists disagree on which effect would weigh most.

c378195.titulo: Ties pension increases to the minimum wage
c378195.oQueMuda: The minimum wage would be the benchmark for adjusting social security benefits and their real value.
c378195.quemAfeta: Retirees and pensioners of the national social security system (INSS).
c378195.porQueImporta: Retirees earning more than the minimum wage would get bigger raises, but social security spending, the largest federal expense, would rise sharply.

c539564.titulo: Guarantees pensions the same increase as the minimum wage
c539564.oQueMuda: No social security benefit could rise less than the minimum wage, and current ones would be updated.
c539564.quemAfeta: Retirees and pensioners of the national social security system.
c539564.porQueImporta: Retirees earning more than the minimum wage would get bigger raises, but social security spending, the largest federal expense, would rise sharply.

c543447.titulo: Protects the real value of pensions
c543447.oQueMuda: Pensions and social security benefits would be guaranteed to keep their purchasing power.
c543447.porQueImporta: Retirees would be protected from inflation losses; the effect on spending depends on the index used, since benefits are already adjusted for inflation today.

c1228532.titulo: Bans moving to lighter prison regimes for heinous crimes and trafficking
c1228532.oQueMuda: People convicted of torture, drug trafficking, terrorism and heinous crimes would serve the whole sentence in the same regime.
c1228532.quemAfeta: People convicted of these crimes and the prison system.
c1228532.porQueImporta: Prisoners convicted of these crimes would serve the full sentence in closed prison, increasing the prison population and costs; the Supreme Court struck down a similar rule in 2006.

c2155899.titulo: Toughens sentences for heinous crimes against military and police
c2155899.oQueMuda: Heinous crimes against military personnel, police and their families would have harsher sentencing rules.
c2155899.quemAfeta: Security agents, their families and convicts.
c2155899.porQueImporta: People convicted of crimes against security officers would stay in prison longer, toughening punishment for this group of victims and increasing the prison population.

s8635009.oQueMuda: Changes the bodies and powers of federal and state military courts.
s8635009.quemAfeta: Military personnel and the military courts.
s8635009.porQueImporta: It would change which cases involving military personnel go to military courts, affecting how crimes by the military, including against civilians, are punished.

c336945.titulo: Allows municipal guards in state capitals to protect people
c336945.oQueMuda: State capitals could have guards to protect people and private property, alongside the military police.
c336945.quemAfeta: Municipal guards and residents of capitals.
c336945.porQueImporta: Guards in state capitals could protect people and private property, expanding policing but using public money for private property security and raising city spending.

c528631.titulo: Limits politicians' raises to the minimum wage increase
c528631.oQueMuda: Salaries of legislators, executives and listed officials could not rise more than the minimum wage.
c528631.porQueImporta: Politicians' salaries could not rise faster than the minimum wage, reducing spending and gaps, but possibly making these posts less attractive and freezing pay for a long time.

c578465.oQueMuda: Creates a civil police in cities and redefines the military police's duties.
c578465.porQueImporta: Cities would have their own civil police, which could bring investigation closer to residents, but would create another costly body and role conflicts with state police.

c2086167.oQueMuda: Cities could have police for patrolling and public order, using municipal guards.
c2086167.porQueImporta: Cities could have police forces, expanding street policing but raising city spending and the need to coordinate with state police.

c2120463.titulo: Freezes elected officials' salaries for 5 years
c2120463.oQueMuda: Salaries of people holding elected office could not rise for five years.
c2120463.porQueImporta: Freezing politicians' salaries for five years cuts spending, but the budget effect is small, since there are few such posts.

c2166332.titulo: Adds municipal police to public safety
c2166332.oQueMuda: Municipal police forces would become part of the public safety bodies.
c2166332.porQueImporta: Municipal police would gain security-force status, expanding policing but also city spending and the need to coordinate with state police.

c2174544.titulo: Adds municipal guards to public safety
c2174544.oQueMuda: Municipal guards would officially become part of the public safety bodies.
c2174544.porQueImporta: Municipal guards would gain security-force status, expanding policing in cities but also city spending and debates over weapons and the limits of their role.

c2227277.titulo: Requires cities over 20,000 people to have a municipal guard
c2227277.oQueMuda: Every city with 20,000 or more residents would have to create a municipal guard.
c2227277.porQueImporta: Hundreds of towns would have to create and pay for a municipal guard, expanding policing but weighing on the finances of mid-sized cities, which already have little money.

c2314519.titulo: Requires reinvesting concession money in transport
c2314519.oQueMuda: At least 70% of what is paid for transport concessions would have to be reinvested in the sector.
c2314519.quemAfeta: Users of highways, ports and railways, and the government.
c2314519.porQueImporta: Concession money would go back into roads, ports and railways, possibly improving infrastructure but leaving less for other areas and for reducing debt.

c2350490.titulo: Adds culture to the social rights
c2350490.oQueMuda: Adds culture to the Constitution's list of social rights (article 6). On its own, it does not create programs, funding or penalties.
c2350490.quemAfeta: The whole population, artists and governments.
c2350490.porQueImporta: The Constitution already tells the State to guarantee cultural rights; the change also puts culture on the list of social rights.

c597232.titulo: Changes the makeup and oversight of audit courts
c597232.oQueMuda: Changes how audit court members are chosen and places them under the CNJ and CNMP councils.
c597232.porQueImporta: Audit Court members, today usually appointed by politicians, would be overseen by national councils, increasing control over those who audit public accounts.

c2478427.titulo: Expands legislators' immunity for what they say
c2478427.oQueMuda: Deputies and senators could not be punished for opinions anywhere, and a Supreme Court justice who disregards this would lose office.
c2478427.porQueImporta: Lawmakers could not be punished for statements anywhere, including on social media, protecting political activity but making it harder to hold them accountable for threats, insults or disinformation; Supreme Court justices acting against this would lose their post.

c2190000.titulo: Increases federal transfers to the FPM
c2190000.oQueMuda: An extra share of federal revenue, including CSLL and Cofins, would go to the Municipal Participation Fund.
c2190000.porQueImporta: City governments would receive more money, and the federal government would keep less for its own spending, including social security, funded by Cofins and CSLL.

c2228314.titulo: Increases the share of federal taxes sent to states and cities
c2228314.oQueMuda: Raises the shares of income tax and IPI revenue passed to states, the Federal District and cities.
c2228314.quemAfeta: States, cities and the federal government.
c2228314.porQueImporta: States and cities would receive more, and the federal government would keep less money for its own spending.

s8759356.titulo: Adds protection of victims to the fundamental rights
s8759356.oQueMuda: States that victims of crimes and public disasters have the right to special protection, as set by law, and bans insufficient protection by the State. On its own, it does not create services or funding: a law is needed.
s8759356.quemAfeta: Victims of crimes and disasters, and the government.
s8759356.porQueImporta: It would give victims a right written in the Constitution to demand protection from the State in court.

s8759452.titulo: Applies the salary cap to allowances too
s8759452.oQueMuda: The public sector salary cap would also apply to allowances and compensation payments.
s8759452.quemAfeta: Civil servants and officials with high salaries.
s8759452.porQueImporta: Allowances and compensation would count toward the salary cap, cutting payments above the limit and reducing spending; careers that receive these amounts would lose part of their income.

c125854.titulo: Expands freedom of association for unions
c125854.oQueMuda: Changes rules on union organization and union contributions.
c125854.porQueImporta: It would change how unions are formed and funded, affecting workers' bargaining power and the power of existing unions.

c2350568.titulo: Requires Congress's approval for public bank loans abroad
c2350568.oQueMuda: Loans by the BNDES and other federal banks for projects abroad would depend on Congress.
c2350568.quemAfeta: Public banks and the federal government.
c2350568.porQueImporta: Loans from public banks for works abroad would depend on Congress, increasing control but possibly delaying Brazilian companies' business abroad.

c2362646.titulo: Allows direct transfers of caucus amendments to states and cities
c2362646.oQueMuda: Individual and caucus budget amendments could be transferred directly, without formal agreements.
c2362646.porQueImporta: Amendment money would reach states and cities faster, but without agreements it becomes harder to know and audit how it was spent.

c2291133.titulo: Bans active-duty military from civilian government posts
c2291133.oQueMuda: Active-duty military could not hold civilian posts in public administration.
c2291133.porQueImporta: Active-duty military personnel could not hold civilian posts, keeping the armed forces out of politics but taking away a source of managers from governments.

c2238418.titulo: Requires collective Supreme Court decisions on injunctions
c2238418.oQueMuda: Injunctions in constitutional challenges would have to be decided by more than one justice.
c2238418.porQueImporta: A single justice could no longer suspend laws alone on an urgent basis, reducing individual rulings but possibly delaying court responses.

s8204843.titulo: Transfers federal seaside land to states, cities and occupants
s8204843.oQueMuda: It abolishes 'marine land' (federal seaside strips): the federal government keeps land in federal use and unoccupied areas; states and municipalities receive areas used for their services; and registered occupants (or those there for at least 5 years) may become owners.
s8204843.quemAfeta: Coastal residents and businesses, states, municipalities and the federal government.
s8204843.porQueImporta: Occupants of seaside land could become owners and stop paying fees to the federal government, which would lose that revenue and control over these areas; part of the debate is whether this would make it easier to privatize beach access.

c2336481.titulo: Allows direct election of the leadership of the largest state courts
c2336481.oQueMuda: In state Courts of Justice with more than 170 appellate judges, all of them would vote by secret ballot to choose the leadership, for 2-year terms with only one re-election.
c2336481.quemAfeta: Appellate judges in the largest state courts, such as São Paulo's.
c2336481.porQueImporta: In large courts, such as São Paulo's, all appellate judges would vote for the leadership, broadening participation but changing a rule that today gives command to the most senior.

c543252.titulo: Guarantees the right to life from conception
c543252.oQueMuda: The Constitution would state that the right to life is inviolable from conception.
c543252.porQueImporta: It could make unconstitutional the cases of abortion allowed by law today, such as rape and risk to the mother's life, and affect embryo research and fertility treatments.

c567421.titulo: Requires a referendum to sell control of state-owned companies
c567421.oQueMuda: Selling control of state-owned companies would require approval by voters in a referendum.
c567421.porQueImporta: Selling state companies would depend on a referendum, giving the public a direct voice but making privatizations costly and much harder.

c1672707.titulo: Bans provisional measures that reduce labor rights
c1672707.oQueMuda: The President could not issue a provisional measure (executive decree) to reduce workers' rights.
c1672707.porQueImporta: Labor rights could only be reduced by a law passed by Congress, giving workers more security but taking away a fast way for the government to change rules in a crisis.

c2211748.titulo: Adds social workers, psychologists and nutritionists to schools
c2211748.oQueMuda: Public and private schools would have these professionals.
c2211748.porQueImporta: Students would have mental health and nutrition support at school, but public systems and private schools would have to hire these professionals, raising costs and fees.

c2186256.titulo: Bans provisional measures on labor and pensions
c2186256.oQueMuda: The President could not issue a provisional measure (executive decree) on labor or pension law.
c2186256.porQueImporta: Changes to labor and pension rules would always depend on Congress, giving workers and retirees more security but taking away a fast way for the government to act in crises, as during the pandemic.

s8743101.titulo: Allows summoning regulatory agencies to Congress
s8743101.oQueMuda: Heads of regulatory agencies and other federal bodies could be summoned to explain themselves.
s8743101.quemAfeta: Agencies such as Anatel, Aneel and ANS.
s8743101.porQueImporta: Congress could compel heads of regulatory agencies to explain themselves, expanding oversight but also political pressure on technical decisions, such as energy tariffs.

c591185.titulo: Simplifies pension contributions for waste pickers
c591185.oQueMuda: Waste pickers who work as a family would contribute to social security as special insured workers.
c591185.porQueImporta: Waste pickers would have easier access to pensions and benefits while paying little, increasing protection for this group and social security spending.

c1732943.titulo: Sets a deadline for Congress to rule on the President's accounts
c1732943.oQueMuda: Congress would have a deadline to rule on the presidential accounts, or the head of Congress would commit an impeachable offense.
c1732943.porQueImporta: Each president's accounts would have to be judged on time, strengthening oversight, since today many go years without a ruling.

s7730684.titulo: Creates 8-year terms for Supreme Court justices
s7730684.oQueMuda: Supreme Court justices would serve eight-year terms, with deadlines for nomination and approval.
s7730684.quemAfeta: Current and future Supreme Court justices.
s7730684.porQueImporta: With eight-year terms, Supreme Court justices would be replaced more often, renewing the court but increasing the number of appointments each president makes.

c2448732.titulo: Lets Congress suspend Supreme Court rulings
c2448732.oQueMuda: Injunctions would have to be confirmed by the full court, and Congress could halt certain Supreme Court rulings.
c2448732.porQueImporta: Congress could overturn certain Supreme Court rulings, increasing elected politicians' power over the courts and weakening the court's role in striking down unconstitutional laws.

c2278136.titulo: Exempts vaccines from taxes in health emergencies
c2278136.oQueMuda: Vaccines and supplies against diseases under a national emergency would be tax-free for three years.
c2278136.quemAfeta: Vaccine makers and the public health system (SUS).
c2278136.porQueImporta: Vaccines in emergencies would be cheaper for the public health system and buyers, with a small, temporary loss of revenue.

s8730454.titulo: Creates a long-term plan to guide the budget
s8730454.oQueMuda: A plan covering several four-year periods would guide federal spending and investment.
s8730454.porQueImporta: A long-term plan would give more continuity to works and investments across governments, but reduces each elected government's freedom to change priorities.

s8735524.titulo: Lets Congress halt acts of other branches
s8735524.oQueMuda: The legislature could annul executive and judicial rules that exceed their powers.
s8735524.quemAfeta: Congress, the government and the courts.
s8735524.porQueImporta: Congress could annul acts by the government and courts it considers excessive, increasing its power over the other branches and possibly creating more conflicts between them.

c459294.titulo: Merges civil and military police and demilitarizes firefighters
c459294.oQueMuda: Creates a single state police force replacing civil and military police and makes firefighters civilian.
c459294.quemAfeta: Police officers, firefighters and municipal guards.
c459294.porQueImporta: A single police force could reduce disputes and duplicated costs between military and civil police, but would require a huge reorganization of careers and face strong resistance from the forces.

c595169.oQueMuda: Adds new state and city police forces to the public safety bodies.
c595169.porQueImporta: Creating new state and municipal police forces expands policing but increases spending and the number of forces that must coordinate.

c2212168.titulo: Limits spending on public debt payments
c2212168.oQueMuda: Adds a limit on public debt spending to the spending cap.
c2212168.porQueImporta: Capping debt payments would free money for other areas, but could worry creditors, make new government borrowing more expensive and affect confidence in the economy.

s8719180.titulo: Guarantees compensation to police injured on duty
s8719180.oQueMuda: Police and state military personnel would be compensated for accidents or assaults suffered at work.
s8719180.quemAfeta: Police and military personnel of the states and the federal government.
s8719180.porQueImporta: Injured police officers would have guaranteed compensation, recognizing the risks of the job and increasing state and federal spending.

s8720944.titulo: Creates a financing fund for the South region
s8720944.oQueMuda: Creates a constitutional fund for the South, focused on Rio Grande do Sul's recovery after the floods.
s8720944.quemAfeta: Companies and residents of the South.
s8720944.porQueImporta: The South would get subsidized credit like the North and Northeast, helping rebuild Rio Grande do Sul but splitting federal funds among more regions.

c1548995.titulo: Shares social contributions with states and cities
c1548995.oQueMuda: Part of CSLL and Cofins revenue would be passed on to states, the Federal District and cities.
c1548995.quemAfeta: States, cities and the federal government.
c1548995.porQueImporta: States and cities would receive more, but social security, funded by CSLL and Cofins, would lose resources for health, pensions and assistance.

c2455515.titulo: Creates a national climate authority, council and fund
c2455515.oQueMuda: Creates the National Climate Change Council, the National Climate Authority and a federally funded fund.
c2455515.porQueImporta: It would create bodies and a fund for climate, which could give continuity to climate policies but increases the size and costs of the federal government.

c2352476.titulo: Pardons parties and reserves funds for Black candidates
c2352476.oQueMuda: Pardons parties that didn't meet gender and race quotas and requires 30% of funds for Black and brown candidates.
c2352476.porQueImporta: Parties would be freed from fines for not meeting quotas for women and Black candidates, weakening these rules; in exchange, there would be a minimum of funding for Black candidates.

s8705604.titulo: Guarantees lawyers the right to speak at any hearing
s8705604.oQueMuda: Lawyers would have the right to oral argument at any hearing in any court.
s8705604.porQueImporta: Lawyers could speak at every hearing, strengthening the defense but slowing down the schedules of courts with thousands of cases.

s8466340.titulo: Adds city attorneys to the public legal service
s8466340.oQueMuda: City attorneys would become part of the public legal service provided for in the Constitution.
s8466340.porQueImporta: Towns would need civil-service attorneys, professionalizing city legal defense but increasing costs, especially in small towns.

c2388029.titulo: Sets aside part of lawmakers' budget amendments for natural disasters
c2388029.oQueMuda: 5% of individual budget amendments from deputies and senators would go to disaster prevention and response, such as floods and droughts.
c2388029.quemAfeta: Municipalities hit by floods, droughts and landslides.
c2388029.porQueImporta: There would be guaranteed money to prevent and respond to disasters, but lawmakers would have less freedom to direct their amendments to other areas.

c2448752.titulo: Defines life as beginning at conception
c2448752.oQueMuda: The Constitution would state that the right to life is inviolable from fertilization.
c2448752.porQueImporta: It could make unconstitutional the cases of abortion allowed by law today, such as rape and risk to the mother's life, and affect embryo research and fertility treatments.

s8693939.oQueMuda: The government would have to carry out budget amendments made by congressional committees.
s8693939.porQueImporta: Lawmakers would control another part of the budget, and the government would have less room to set priorities and cut spending when money is short.

s8693978.titulo: Creates the Rio Grande do Sul Free Trade Zone
s8693978.oQueMuda: Creates, for a set period, an area with tax benefits in Rio Grande do Sul.
s8693978.quemAfeta: Companies and residents of Rio Grande do Sul.
s8693978.porQueImporta: Companies would pay lower taxes in Rio Grande do Sul, which could help recovery after the floods but reduces revenue and may draw companies from other states.

c2189078.titulo: Changes how the State Participation Fund is shared
c2189078.oQueMuda: Changes the rules for splitting the FPE among states and the Federal District.
c2189078.porQueImporta: Changing how FPE (federal transfers to states) is split takes money from some states to give to others; for poorer states, this transfer is a major source of revenue.

c2209439.titulo: Allows regional funds to pay for public works
c2209439.oQueMuda: Money from the North, Northeast and Center-West funds could finance public works.
c2209439.quemAfeta: States and cities in these regions.
c2209439.porQueImporta: Governments in the North, Northeast and Center-West could use these funds for public works, but less cheap credit would remain for companies and producers in these regions.

s8582100.oQueMuda: Increases the length of maternity, paternity and adoption leave.
s8582100.porQueImporta: Parents would have more time with their children, which could share care more evenly; the cost would fall on social security and on companies, which go longer without the employee.

c2277279.titulo: Makes access to drinking water a fundamental right
c2277279.oQueMuda: Access to drinking water would be included among fundamental rights.
c2277279.quemAfeta: People without clean water and the government.
c2277279.porQueImporta: It would give a constitutional basis for demanding that governments provide clean water; on its own, it does not create funding or works.

c2147461.titulo: Removes the time limit to prosecute rape
c2147461.oQueMuda: Rape could be punished at any time.
c2147461.quemAfeta: Victims and those accused of rape.
c2147461.porQueImporta: Rape suspects could be prosecuted at any time, which favors victims who take time to report; on the other hand, evidence of very old events is harder to produce and contest.

s7755772.titulo: Limits expropriations and requires market-price compensation
s7755772.oQueMuda: Expropriating urban and rural property would need approval from the legislature or a court, with payment at market value.
s7755772.quemAfeta: Owners, governments and housing and land movements.
s7755772.porQueImporta: Expropriating land and property would become more expensive and slower, protecting owners but making land reform and affordable housing projects harder.

c2229539.titulo: Removes the time limit to prosecute rape and femicide
c2229539.oQueMuda: Rape and femicide would allow no bail and could be punished at any time.
c2229539.quemAfeta: Victims, their families and the accused.
c2229539.porQueImporta: People accused of rape and femicide could be prosecuted at any time, favoring victims and families, but evidence of very old events is harder to produce and contest.

c451074.oQueMuda: People not affiliated with a party could run for office.
c451074.porQueImporta: People outside parties could run for office, widening voters' choices but possibly fragmenting Congress further and weakening parties.

c2140427.oQueMuda: Defines how voters can revoke terms through a citizen initiative.
c2140427.porQueImporta: Voters could remove politicians before the end of their term, increasing popular control but also instability and the cost of new votes.

c2145346.titulo: Allows independent candidates and civic lists
c2145346.oQueMuda: Candidates without a party could run with voter support and join civic lists.
c2145346.porQueImporta: Candidates without a party could run, widening voters' choices but possibly fragmenting Congress further and weakening parties.

c2162013.titulo: Allows candidates without a party with support from 1% of voters
c2162013.oQueMuda: Anyone backed by 1% of voters could run without a party.
c2162013.porQueImporta: Candidates without a party could run, widening voters' choices but possibly fragmenting Congress further and weakening parties.

c2226594.oQueMuda: The government would be led by a prime minister with the support of Congress.
c2226594.porQueImporta: The government would depend on congressional support and could fall without an election, making it easier to replace unpopular governments but possibly creating more instability in a Congress with many parties; in 1993 the country chose presidentialism in a referendum.

s8670175.titulo: Adds sport to the social rights
s8670175.oQueMuda: Adds sport to the Constitution's list of social rights (article 6). On its own, it does not create programs, funding or penalties.
s8670175.quemAfeta: The whole population, athletes and governments.
s8670175.porQueImporta: The Constitution already says the State must encourage sport; the change also puts it on the list of social rights.

c2153455.oQueMuda: Creates security bodies for juvenile detention centers.
c2153455.quemAfeta: Juvenile detention staff and detained teenagers.
c2153455.porQueImporta: Juvenile detention staff would gain security status, which may bring career advantages, and brings the treatment of teenagers closer to a police approach.

c2436619.titulo: Adds integration with Portuguese-speaking countries to foreign policy
c2436619.oQueMuda: States that Brazil will seek economic, political, social and cultural integration with Portuguese-speaking countries, to form a lusophone community. On its own, it does not create programs, funding or penalties.
c2436619.porQueImporta: The Constitution already has a similar rule for Latin America; this would also guide foreign policy toward Portuguese-speaking countries.

s8655096.titulo: Creates a special fiscal regime for environmental disasters
s8655096.oQueMuda: Governments could relax fiscal and procurement rules to deal with regional or local disasters.
s8655096.quemAfeta: Residents of affected areas and governments.
s8655096.porQueImporta: Governments could spend and hire faster in disasters, but with fewer controls, increasing the risk of poorly managed spending.

s8394295.titulo: Creates a length-of-service bonus for judges and prosecutors
s8394295.oQueMuda: Judges and prosecutors would receive an extra payment every five years of service.
s8394295.porQueImporta: Judges and prosecutors, already among the highest-paid public servants, would get an automatic bonus, costing billions a year for the federal government and states.

s8572569.titulo: Removes the time limit to prosecute child trafficking
s8572569.oQueMuda: Trafficking of children and teenagers could be punished at any time.
s8572569.quemAfeta: Victims and those accused of this crime.
s8572569.porQueImporta: People accused of child trafficking could be prosecuted at any time, which favors victims who can only report as adults.

c2329063.titulo: Bans cutting the armed forces' budget
c2329063.oQueMuda: Removes limits and bans freezes on armed forces funding.
c2329063.quemAfeta: The armed forces and the federal budget.
c2329063.porQueImporta: The armed forces would be protected from cuts, giving predictability to defense projects but forcing the government to cut more elsewhere when money is short.

s8060121.titulo: Adds the right to clean air to the fundamental rights
s8060121.oQueMuda: States that everyone has the right to air quality, including in shared indoor spaces, public or private. On its own, it does not create programs, funding or penalties.
s8060121.quemAfeta: The whole population, companies and governments.
s8060121.porQueImporta: The Constitution already guarantees a balanced environment; the change mentions air explicitly, which can be used in laws and in court.

s8646008.titulo: Changes small business taxation under the tax reform
s8646008.oQueMuda: Fixes rules of the new tax system for micro and small businesses and individual micro-entrepreneurs (MEIs).
s8646008.quemAfeta: Micro and small businesses and individual micro-entrepreneurs.
s8646008.porQueImporta: Small businesses and micro-entrepreneurs could pay less and face less red tape in the new system, but each special treatment tends to raise the rate paid by everyone else.

s8644146.titulo: Sends part of tourism sales tax back to the sector
s8644146.oQueMuda: States would set aside a share of ICMS from tourism services to promote tourism.
s8644146.quemAfeta: The tourism sector and state governments.
s8644146.porQueImporta: Tourism would have guaranteed funding, but less ICMS would remain for health, education and security in the states.

s8639865.titulo: Adds culture to the social rights
s8639865.oQueMuda: Adds culture to the Constitution's list of social rights (article 6). On its own, it does not create programs, funding or penalties.
s8639865.quemAfeta: The whole population, artists and governments.
s8639865.porQueImporta: The Constitution already tells the State to guarantee cultural rights; the change also puts culture on the list of social rights.

c2017887.titulo: Lets Congress halt acts of the judiciary
c2017887.oQueMuda: Congress could annul rules issued by the judiciary.
c2017887.porQueImporta: Congress could annul rules issued by the judiciary, increasing its power over the courts and possibly creating more conflicts between branches.

c2207351.titulo: Lets Congress halt acts of the judiciary
c2207351.oQueMuda: Congress could annul judiciary rules it considers excessive.
c2207351.porQueImporta: Congress could annul judicial rules it considers excessive, increasing its power over the courts and possibly creating more conflicts between branches.

c344176.titulo: Extends special retirement to education professionals
c344176.oQueMuda: Those in teaching or teaching support would have five years off the required age and contribution time.
c344176.porQueImporta: More education staff would retire earlier, recognizing these roles but increasing pension spending by states and municipalities.

c400327.titulo: Counts teaching in hospitals and prisons as teaching service
c400327.oQueMuda: Teachers in hospitals, rehabilitation centers and prisons would have special retirement.
c400327.porQueImporta: Teachers in hospitals and prisons would retire earlier, recognizing this work but increasing public pension spending.

c415712.titulo: Ends the minimum retirement age for teachers
c415712.oQueMuda: Public school teachers could retire based only on contribution time, with no minimum age.
c415712.porQueImporta: Teachers could retire younger, which may worsen teacher shortages and increases pension spending by states and municipalities.

c489706.titulo: Counts time in former daycare centers toward retirement
c489706.oQueMuda: Early childhood teachers could count time worked in daycare centers before they joined school systems.
c489706.porQueImporta: Early childhood teachers could retire earlier, correcting a loss for this group and increasing municipal pension spending.

c2117201.titulo: Adds municipal guards to public safety
c2117201.oQueMuda: Municipal guards would become part of the public safety bodies, with retirement rights.
c2117201.porQueImporta: Municipal guards would gain security-force status and special retirement, expanding policing but increasing costs and city pension deficits.

c349704.titulo: Gives severance fund (FGTS) and unemployment insurance to political appointees
c349704.oQueMuda: Civil servants in freely appointed posts would be entitled to notice, the FGTS severance fund and unemployment insurance.
c349704.porQueImporta: Political appointees would get severance funds and unemployment insurance when dismissed, giving them protection but raising the cost of each appointed post for governments.

s7826575.oQueMuda: Fathers and mothers could alternate and share the days of maternity leave.
s7826575.porQueImporta: Fathers could spend more time with the baby and mothers could return to work sooner if they wish, which may reduce hiring discrimination against women.

s7830951.titulo: Requires Congress's approval for Brazil to leave treaties
s7830951.oQueMuda: Brazil could only withdraw from an international treaty with Congress's prior approval.
s7830951.porQueImporta: Leaving international agreements, such as on climate or human rights, would depend on Congress, giving more stability but reducing the president's freedom in foreign policy.

s7856184.titulo: Replaces maternity leave with 180-day parental leave
s7856184.oQueMuda: Creates a 180-day leave that fathers and mothers, including adoptive parents, could share.
s7856184.porQueImporta: Parents could share 180 days of leave, spreading care and possibly reducing discrimination against women; costs for social security and companies would rise.

c2024222.titulo: Broadens the definition of family in the Constitution
c2024222.oQueMuda: A family would be any group of two or more people joined by blood, affection, marriage or civil union.
c2024222.porQueImporta: Families of various kinds, such as those formed by affection, would have inheritance, pension and benefit rights recognized in the Constitution, ending court disputes but touching on religious and political disagreement.

c2221375.titulo: Creates a fund for a possible state formed by merging with the former capital
c2221375.oQueMuda: Creates a constitutional fund for a federal unit resulting from a merger with the former capital and sets a 10-year limit for these funds.
c2221375.quemAfeta: Residents and the government of Rio de Janeiro.
c2221375.porQueImporta: It would change federal transfers linked to Rio de Janeiro as the former capital, affecting state and federal finances.

c2222665.titulo: Changes the rule on council members holding two jobs
c2222665.oQueMuda: Changes the rule that lets city council members combine their term with a job in city government.
c2222665.quemAfeta: City council members who are civil servants.
c2222665.porQueImporta: It would change who can be a city councilor and hold a city government post at the same time, affecting the council's independence from the mayor.

c2224677.titulo: Expands the state's duty in education
c2224677.oQueMuda: Adds a new state duty toward education and changes a school funding rule.
c2224677.porQueImporta: A new State duty in education may require more spending, without saying where the money would come from.

c2084719.titulo: Guarantees civil servants a yearly raise at least equal to inflation
c2084719.oQueMuda: The general annual salary review for civil servants could not be lower than inflation.
c2084719.porQueImporta: Civil servants would have guaranteed inflation-linked raises every year, protecting their salaries but making budgets more rigid and squeezing other spending in crisis years.

s8412320.titulo: Details the right to food with the idea of food security
s8412320.oQueMuda: States that the right to food includes regular and permanent access to enough safe and healthy food for everyone. On its own, it does not create programs, funding or penalties.
s8412320.quemAfeta: People facing food insecurity and governments.
s8412320.porQueImporta: Food has been a social right since 2010; the change explains in the Constitution what that right means.

s8623312.titulo: Expands legislators' immunity for their opinions
s8623312.oQueMuda: Reworks the rule so deputies and senators can't be punished for opinions and votes anywhere.
s8623312.porQueImporta: Lawmakers could not be punished for statements anywhere, including social media, protecting political activity but making it harder to hold them accountable for threats, insults or disinformation.

s8622879.titulo: Requires a verifiable printed ballot in elections
