s8622879.oQueMuda: Voting machines would have to print a ballot the voter checks, which is kept for audits.
s8622879.porQueImporta: Printing votes would allow paper recounts but would cost billions in printers and logistics and bring risks of failures and breaches of ballot secrecy; the Supreme Court struck down a similar rule in 2020.

s8617172.titulo: Lowers the age of criminal responsibility to 16 for heinous crimes
s8617172.oQueMuda: 16 and 17-year-olds who commit heinous crimes would be tried as adults.
s8617172.porQueImporta: 16- and 17-year-olds would go to adult prisons for heinous crimes, toughening punishment but placing them in overcrowded prisons where gangs recruit inmates.

s8620564.titulo: Lets Congress halt acts of the judiciary and councils
s8620564.oQueMuda: Congress could annul acts of courts and councils that exceed their powers.
s8620564.quemAfeta: Congress, the courts, the CNJ and the CNMP.
s8620564.porQueImporta: Congress could annul rules issued by courts and councils, increasing its power over the judiciary and prosecutors and possibly creating more conflicts between branches.

c2196833.titulo: Tax reform: replaces five taxes with IBS and CBS
c2196833.oQueMuda: Replaces PIS, Cofins, IPI, ICMS and ISS with two consumption taxes, the IBS and the CBS, plus a selective tax.
c2196833.porQueImporta: Already in force (Amendment 132): it simplifies consumption taxes from 2026, with a transition until 2033; some sectors pay more and others less, and it changes how much each state collects.

s8403380.titulo: Adjusts federal transfers to cities for inflation
s8403380.oQueMuda: Amounts in federal agreements and programs with cities would be updated for inflation.
s8403380.porQueImporta: City governments would receive inflation-adjusted amounts in federal programs, keeping their purchasing power but increasing federal spending.

c459272.titulo: Aligns the Constitution with the UN disability convention
c459272.oQueMuda: Updates several articles to follow the UN Convention on the Rights of Persons with Disabilities.
c459272.porQueImporta: It would update terms and rights of people with disabilities in the Constitution; the UN Convention has already had the force of a constitutional amendment since 2008.

s8609290.oQueMuda: People not affiliated with a party could run for office.
s8609290.porQueImporta: People outside parties could run for office, widening voters' choices but possibly fragmenting Congress further and weakening parties.

s8609795.titulo: Grants amnesty for the January 8 riots and restores rights and mandates
s8609795.oQueMuda: It grants amnesty to those involved in the January 8, 2023 riots, restores the rights of those made ineligible over 2022 election conduct and gives back revoked mandates.
s8609795.quemAfeta: People convicted or investigated over the riots and politicians declared ineligible or removed from office.
s8609795.porQueImporta: It would cancel court convictions for the 2023 attacks on the seats of the three branches and restore political rights to those made ineligible, including prominent politicians; critics say this weakens punishment and may encourage new attacks on institutions, while supporters say it would pacify the country.

s8610921.titulo: Ends secret votes in the legislature
s8610921.oQueMuda: All votes in Congress, state assemblies and city councils would be open.
s8610921.porQueImporta: Voters could see how each lawmaker voted on everything, including vetoes and expulsions, increasing transparency but exposing lawmakers to pressure on sensitive votes.

c1555270.titulo: Adds accessibility and urban mobility to the social rights
c1555270.oQueMuda: Adds 'accessibility' and 'urban mobility' to the list of social rights. On its own, it does not create programs, funding or penalties.
c1555270.quemAfeta: People with disabilities or reduced mobility, transport users and city governments.
c1555270.porQueImporta: The Constitution already covers accessibility for people with disabilities and, since 2015, includes transport as a social right.

c2301270.titulo: Adds accessibility and mobility to the fundamental rights
c2301270.oQueMuda: Adds to the list of fundamental rights: 'everyone is guaranteed the right to accessibility and mobility'. On its own, it does not create programs, funding or penalties.
c2301270.quemAfeta: People with disabilities or reduced mobility, and the government.
c2301270.porQueImporta: The Constitution already covers accessibility for people with disabilities; the change turns it into a fundamental right for everyone.

c117100.titulo: Bans workplace discrimination based on sexual orientation and other grounds
c117100.oQueMuda: Bans differences in pay, role and hiring based on sexual orientation, ethnicity, religion, politics or disability.
c117100.porQueImporta: It would expand protection against workplace discrimination in the Constitution; today some of these protections already exist in laws and Supreme Court rulings.

c2195689.titulo: Gives children with disabilities priority in early education
c2195689.oQueMuda: Children with disabilities would have priority for daycare and preschool places.
c2195689.quemAfeta: Children with disabilities and their families.
c2195689.porQueImporta: Children with disabilities would be guaranteed places first, favoring inclusion but possibly lengthening the wait for other children where places are scarce.

c421307.titulo: Passes part of import tax to cities with customs zones
c421307.oQueMuda: 5% of the import tax would go to cities that host customs zones.
c421307.porQueImporta: Cities with ports and borders would gain revenue, and the federal government would keep less import duty.

s8607959.titulo: Bars reducing a legal minimum wage by agreement
s8607959.oQueMuda: Minimum salaries set by law could not be reduced by collective agreements.
s8607959.quemAfeta: Workers with a legal minimum salary and employers.
s8607959.porQueImporta: Professions with a legal pay floor would be protected from cuts by agreement, but companies would have less room to negotiate in crises and avoid layoffs.

c259094.oQueMuda: Changes several parts of the tax system, in a smaller version of tax reform.
c259094.quemAfeta: Taxpayers, states and the federal government.
c259094.porQueImporta: It would change several tax rules at once, affecting how much companies and citizens pay and how much each government collects; part of this debate was overtaken by the 2023 reform.

c536019.titulo: Charges vehicle tax (IPVA) on planes, private jets and boats
c536019.oQueMuda: The IPVA would also apply to aircraft and boats.
c536019.quemAfeta: Owners of planes, helicopters, yachts and motorboats.
c536019.porQueImporta: Owners of private jets, helicopters, yachts and speedboats would pay vehicle tax like car owners; the 2023 tax reform already allowed this charge.

c582954.titulo: Expands the vehicle tax (IPVA) and creates exemptions
c582954.oQueMuda: The IPVA would apply to more vehicles and be banned in some situations.
c582954.porQueImporta: More vehicles would pay IPVA and some would be exempt, changing who pays and how much states and cities collect.

c2081040.titulo: Sets a deadline to enact constitutional amendments
c2081040.oQueMuda: Approved amendments would have a deadline to be enacted.
c2081040.porQueImporta: Amendments passed by Congress could not be left unenacted, preventing Congress's leadership from blocking changes already voted.

c2189052.titulo: Makes newly sworn-in deputies and senators lose any other office
c2189052.oQueMuda: On taking office as deputy or senator, a person would permanently lose any other elected office they held.
c2189052.quemAfeta: Officeholders who are elected to Congress.
c2189052.porQueImporta: Anyone elected to Congress would lose their previous mandate, such as city councilor, preventing post-switching but possibly discouraging candidacies.

c2404706.titulo: Allows using leftover COVID funds for health
c2404706.oQueMuda: Leftover federal funds sent to fight the pandemic could be used for other health actions.
c2404706.quemAfeta: States, cities and patients of the public health system (SUS).
c2404706.porQueImporta: States and cities could use leftover pandemic money for other health actions, freeing resources without increasing federal spending.

c2406638.titulo: Creates a specific legal regime for police officers
c2406638.oQueMuda: Sets specific rules on careers, retirement and survivor pensions for police.
c2406638.porQueImporta: Police would have their own career and retirement rules, usually more favorable, increasing pension spending and setting a precedent for other careers.

c2405983.titulo: Swaps payroll contributions for a transactions tax
c2405983.oQueMuda: Contributions on payroll and revenue would be replaced by a charge on financial transactions.
c2405983.porQueImporta: Hiring would become cheaper, which could encourage jobs, but the new tax would be charged on every bank transaction, including those of the poorest, like the old CPMF.

c530024.titulo: Lets foreigners vote and run in municipal elections
c530024.oQueMuda: Foreigners living in Brazil could take part in municipal elections.
c530024.porQueImporta: Immigrants living in Brazil would have a say in their city's elections, expanding participation but changing the rule that only Brazilian citizens vote.

c599448.titulo: Lets foreigners who have lived in Brazil over four years vote
c599448.oQueMuda: Foreign residents with regular status living in Brazil for more than four years could vote.
c599448.porQueImporta: Immigrants with more than four years in the country could vote, expanding participation but changing the rule that only Brazilian citizens vote.

c2162990.titulo: Gives voting rights to foreigners who have lived in Brazil over five years
c2162990.oQueMuda: Foreigners legally residing in Brazil for more than five years could vote.
c2162990.porQueImporta: Immigrants with more than five years in the country could vote, expanding participation but changing the rule that only Brazilian citizens vote.

c2196315.titulo: Lets military personnel return to active duty after a term
c2196315.oQueMuda: Elected military personnel could return to active service when their term ends.
c2196315.quemAfeta: Military personnel who run for office.
c2196315.porQueImporta: Military personnel could go into politics and then return to the barracks, making candidacies easier but bringing the armed forces closer to party politics.

s8580579.titulo: Requires Congress's approval for binding Supreme Court precedents
s8580579.oQueMuda: The Supreme Court's binding precedents would be reviewed by Congress.
s8580579.porQueImporta: Congress would have the final say on Supreme Court rulings binding all judges, increasing politicians' power over the courts and possibly delaying uniform decisions.

s8582557.titulo: Requires Congress's approval to recognize Indigenous lands
s8582557.oQueMuda: Recognition of Indigenous lands would have to be approved by Congress.
s8582557.porQueImporta: Demarcating Indigenous lands would depend on Congress, where the agribusiness caucus is strong; this tends to reduce new demarcations and gives farmers in disputed areas more security.

s8582970.titulo: Makes child sexual abuse a crime without bail or time limit
s8582970.oQueMuda: Child sexual abuse crimes would allow no bail and could be punished at any time.
s8582970.quemAfeta: Victims and those accused of these crimes.
s8582970.porQueImporta: People accused of sexual crimes against children could be prosecuted at any time and denied bail, favoring victims who only report as adults.

s8583613.titulo: Requires Congress's approval to recognize Indigenous lands
s8583613.oQueMuda: Recognition of Indigenous lands would depend on approval by Congress.
s8583613.porQueImporta: Demarcating Indigenous lands would depend on Congress, where the agribusiness caucus is strong; this tends to reduce new demarcations and gives farmers in disputed areas more security.

c553109.titulo: Requires a degree to work as a journalist
c553109.oQueMuda: Again requires a university degree to work as a journalist.
c553109.porQueImporta: Only journalism graduates could work in the profession, valuing the degree but restricting who can work in the press; the Supreme Court struck down this requirement in 2009 as a limit on free expression.

c1724712.titulo: Compensates owners of land declared Indigenous
c1724712.oQueMuda: Owners holding titles to areas declared Indigenous from 2013 onward could be compensated.
c1724712.porQueImporta: Owners with titles to land declared Indigenous would be compensated, reducing conflicts and losses but creating a high cost for the federal government and possibly making demarcations more expensive.

c2288318.titulo: Allows dual citizenship without losing Brazilian nationality
c2288318.oQueMuda: Brazilians would not lose their nationality when acquiring another, unless they ask to.
c2288318.porQueImporta: Already in force (Amendment 131): Brazilians who naturalize in another country no longer lose Brazilian nationality unless they ask to.

c621519.titulo: Gives permanent status to public workers hired without an exam
c621519.oQueMuda: People working for federal, state and city governments would be made permanent civil servants.
c621519.quemAfeta: Temporary and outsourced public sector workers.
c621519.porQueImporta: Thousands of people would become civil servants without a public exam, giving this group stability but increasing staff costs and breaking the rule of equal access through public exams.

c2224532.titulo: Allows judges to swap posts between different courts
c2224532.oQueMuda: Judges could request a transfer or swap posts with colleagues in other courts of the same branch: state, federal or labor courts.
c2224532.porQueImporta: Already in force (Amendment 130): judges can swap courts with colleagues in the same branch, making it easier to move but possibly increasing turnover in inland districts.

s8488781.titulo: Raises science investment to 2.5% of GDP
s8488781.oQueMuda: Investment in science, technology and innovation would gradually rise to at least 2.5% of GDP.
s8488781.porQueImporta: More money for science could bring innovation and long-term growth, but requires billions more per year, which would have to come from other areas or higher taxes.

c407657.titulo: Creates a fund to revitalize the São Francisco River
c407657.oQueMuda: Creates a fund to restore the environment and develop the São Francisco River basin.
c407657.quemAfeta: Residents of the São Francisco basin.
c407657.porQueImporta: The São Francisco River would have guaranteed funding for recovery, but this money would come from taxes that today fund other areas.

c483817.titulo: Makes the Cerrado and the Caatinga national heritage
c483817.oQueMuda: These two biomes would be added to the national heritage areas.
c483817.quemAfeta: Residents and producers in the Cerrado and the Caatinga.
c483817.porQueImporta: Use of the Cerrado and Caatinga would be conditioned on preservation, like the Amazon, strengthening protection but possibly limiting agribusiness expansion in these regions.

s8569449.oQueMuda: The federal government would top up the Municipal Participation Fund to keep the same share of GDP as in 2022.
s8569449.porQueImporta: City governments would be protected from drops in FPM, and the federal government would have to cover the difference with its own money.

c398998.titulo: Ends the 'constitutional fifth' in the courts
c398998.oQueMuda: Courts would no longer reserve seats for lawyers and prosecutors.
c398998.porQueImporta: Courts would be made up only of career judges, valuing the judiciary but removing the diversity brought by lawyers and prosecutors and reducing political influence in appointments.

s7720809.titulo: Guarantees a full public health team for pregnant women
s7720809.oQueMuda: The public health system (SUS) would have to provide a pediatrician, gynecologist, obstetrician, nurses and psychologist during prenatal care, birth and postpartum.
s7720809.porQueImporta: Pregnant women would have a full team in the public health system, which could reduce maternal and infant deaths, but requires hiring professionals nationwide, which is costly and hard in small towns.

c2092664.titulo: Reserves 10% of individual amendments for public safety
c2092664.oQueMuda: 10% of legislators' individual budget amendments would go to public safety.
c2092664.porQueImporta: Security would have guaranteed funding through budget amendments, but less amendment money would be left for other areas, such as health and public works.

s8560990.titulo: Creates 15-year terms for Supreme Court justices
s8560990.oQueMuda: Supreme Court justices would serve 15-year terms with a minimum age of 50, with changes to how higher courts are chosen.
s8560990.quemAfeta: Justices of the Supreme Court and higher courts.
s8560990.porQueImporta: With 15-year terms, Supreme Court justices would be replaced more regularly, renewing the court but changing how many appointments each president makes.

s8242831.titulo: Allows public and private companies to collect and process plasma
s8242831.oQueMuda: It allows public and private entities to collect, process and sell human plasma to make medicines, preferably for the public health system (SUS).
s8242831.quemAfeta: Blood donors, patients and Hemobrás (the state blood products company).
s8242831.porQueImporta: Companies could buy and process plasma, which could increase drug production in the country, but opens room to pay donors and compete with Hemobrás, breaking the rule that blood is not for sale.

s8442337.oQueMuda: Sets institutional rules for the prosecutors who work with the Courts of Accounts.
s8442337.quemAfeta: Audit prosecutors and Courts of Accounts.
s8442337.porQueImporta: Audit prosecutors would gain more independence to oversee public spending, but the oversight structure would become more expensive.

c406708.titulo: Sets aside budget money for affordable housing
c406708.oQueMuda: Federal, state and city governments would have to allocate fixed funds to social housing funds.
c406708.quemAfeta: Families without adequate housing and governments.
c406708.porQueImporta: Affordable housing would have fixed funding every year, giving continuity to housing programs but reducing budget room for other areas.

s8513795.titulo: Tax reform abolishing the ICMS and Cide
s8513795.oQueMuda: Abolishes taxes such as the ICMS and Cide and creates new state tax rules.
s8513795.porQueImporta: It would abolish ICMS and change state taxes, which could simplify the system but affects states' main revenue; the 2023 reform already deals with this using another model.

s8549385.titulo: Extends the right to life to the unborn
s8549385.oQueMuda: The right to life would protect the embryo from conception.
s8549385.porQueImporta: It could make unconstitutional the cases of abortion allowed by law today, such as rape and risk to the mother's life, and affect embryo research and fertility treatments.

s8545103.titulo: Bans charging union fees to non-members
s8545103.oQueMuda: Unions could only charge non-members with their prior individual consent.
s8545103.porQueImporta: Non-member workers would only pay unions if they authorized it, protecting their pay but reducing money for unions that negotiate raises for the whole profession.

s8539271.titulo: Requires Supreme Court justices to face a new hearing every 8 years
s8539271.oQueMuda: The Senate would hold a public hearing of Supreme Court justices every eight years.
s8539271.quemAfeta: Supreme Court justices and the Senate.
s8539271.porQueImporta: Supreme Court justices would periodically have to explain themselves to the Senate, increasing political control over the court and possibly pressuring its rulings.

s8538765.titulo: Temporarily raises transfers to the FPM
s8538765.oQueMuda: Raises for a period the share of income tax and IPI that goes to the Municipal Participation Fund.
s8538765.porQueImporta: City governments would receive more for a period, and the federal government would keep less for its own spending.

s8540424.titulo: Bars judges from cases handled by relatives' law firms
s8540424.oQueMuda: Judges could not rule on cases with lawyers who are their spouses or close relatives.
s8540424.porQueImporta: Judges could not rule on cases with related lawyers, reducing conflicts of interest; the Supreme Court has already ruled on the matter, and the change would put it in the Constitution.

s7723044.titulo: Guarantees cities the ICMS and IPVA that states fail to pass on
s7723044.oQueMuda: The federal government would withhold state funds and pay cities directly the share of ICMS and IPVA not passed on.
s7723044.porQueImporta: Cities would receive their share of ICMS and IPVA even if the state is late, protecting city governments but taking money from states in crisis.

s8326366.titulo: Guarantees free public transit on election day
s8326366.oQueMuda: Buses, boats and intercity transport would be free on voting days.
s8326366.porQueImporta: More low-income voters could get to the polls, possibly reducing abstention; the cost of free transport would fall on governments or transport companies.

c2223558.titulo: Exempts Brazilian-made musical instruments from taxes
c2223558.oQueMuda: Musical instruments made in Brazil would be tax-free.
c2223558.porQueImporta: Brazilian-made instruments would become cheaper, helping musicians and domestic manufacturers, with a small loss of revenue.

c2225811.oQueMuda: Creates a new case in which Brazilians who naturalize through marriage keep their nationality.
c2225811.porQueImporta: Brazilians married to foreigners would not lose their nationality when naturalizing; Amendment 131 of 2023 already guaranteed this more broadly.

s8520995.titulo: Changes how Congress's internal rules are amended
s8520995.oQueMuda: Sets how bills changing the internal rules of the Chamber and Senate are voted on.
s8520995.porQueImporta: It would change how the Chamber and Senate change their own operating rules, affecting the power of the heads of each house and of minorities.

c1555497.titulo: Adds internet access and message privacy to the fundamental rights
c1555497.oQueMuda: Guarantees everyone internet access and the confidentiality of digital communications, which could only be broken by court order in criminal investigations. On its own, it does not create programs, funding or penalties.
c1555497.quemAfeta: Internet users, technology companies and the police.
c1555497.porQueImporta: Confidentiality of communications is already in the Constitution; the change mentions the internet explicitly.

s8513844.titulo: Guarantees free transit for low-income people with disabilities
s8513844.oQueMuda: Low-income people with disabilities would ride urban public transit for free.
s8513844.quemAfeta: People with disabilities and city governments.
s8513844.porQueImporta: Low-income people with disabilities would ride free in all cities, making work and health care easier, but the cost would fall on city governments or paying passengers.

s8513893.titulo: Requires a verifiable printed ballot in elections
s8513893.oQueMuda: Voting machines would have to print a ballot the voter can check, kept for audits.
s8513893.porQueImporta: Printing votes would allow paper recounts but would cost billions in printers and logistics and bring risks of failures and breaches of ballot secrecy; the Supreme Court struck down a similar rule in 2020.

s8386303.titulo: Adds military court judges to the CNJ
s8386303.oQueMuda: Military court judges would get a seat on the National Council of Justice.
s8386303.quemAfeta: The military courts and the CNJ.
s8386303.porQueImporta: Military courts would gain a voice in the body that oversees the judiciary, changing the balance of who decides punishments and rules for judges.

c1738814.oQueMuda: Guarantees extra operating time for lottery outlet permits.
c1738814.porQueImporta: Current lottery outlets would get more time without a new tender, protecting owners and jobs but delaying competition that could bring in others.

s8488965.titulo: Changes the process for provisional measures
s8488965.oQueMuda: Changes deadlines, agenda locking and reissuing of provisional measures (executive decrees).
s8488965.porQueImporta: The president would have less room to govern by provisional measures, giving Congress more power but possibly delaying quick government responses.

s8489404.titulo: Makes the Caatinga, Cerrado and Pampa national heritage
s8489404.oQueMuda: These three biomes would be added to the national heritage areas.
s8489404.quemAfeta: Residents and producers in these biomes.
s8489404.porQueImporta: Use of the Caatinga, Cerrado and Pampa would be conditioned on preservation, like the Amazon, strengthening protection but possibly limiting agribusiness expansion in these regions.

c2118343.titulo: Limits civil servants' vacation to 30 days
c2118343.oQueMuda: All public employees would have 30 days of vacation a year, with one-third extra pay.
c2118343.quemAfeta: Civil servants, including judges and prosecutors.
c2118343.porQueImporta: Judges, prosecutors and other careers with 60 days of vacation would have 30, reducing spending and bringing rules closer to those for other workers.

c139244.titulo: Direct election of state attorneys general
c139244.oQueMuda: The heads of state prosecutors' offices would be elected by prosecutors themselves.
c139244.porQueImporta: Prosecutors would choose their own head, giving prosecutors more independence from the governor but reducing elected officials' control.

c2152285.titulo: Creates a democracy fund financed by politicians' salaries
c2152285.oQueMuda: Politicians and appointees would pay a contribution on their salaries to a fund financing democracy.
c2152285.quemAfeta: Elected politicians and holders of appointed posts.
c2152285.porQueImporta: Politicians and appointees would pay a contribution to fund campaigns, reducing use of other public money, but the amount raised would be small compared with election costs.

s8472168.titulo: Puts mental integrity and algorithm transparency into the Constitution
s8472168.oQueMuda: States that scientific and technological development must ensure people's mental integrity and the transparency of algorithms, as set by law. On its own, it does not create rules for companies: a law is needed.
s8472168.quemAfeta: Technology users, digital companies and lawmakers.
s8472168.porQueImporta: It would give a constitutional basis for future laws on artificial intelligence and neurotechnology.

c1050543.titulo: Allows seizing assets from crime or corruption
c1050543.oQueMuda: Prosecutors and government attorneys could ask courts to seize assets from crime, misconduct or illicit enrichment.
c1050543.quemAfeta: People with assets of illicit origin.
c1050543.porQueImporta: It would become easier to seize assets from those who got rich through crime or corruption, even without a criminal conviction, helping recover diverted money but requiring care not to punish the innocent.

c427297.titulo: Guarantees night-shift pay to police and firefighters
c427297.oQueMuda: Military police, firefighters and other security agents would be entitled to night-shift pay.
c427297.porQueImporta: Security officers who work at night would earn more, recognizing this work and increasing state staff spending.

c1278930.titulo: Sets working hours for military police and firefighters
c1278930.oQueMuda: Defines daily and weekly working hours for military police and firefighters.
c1278930.porQueImporta: Police and firefighters would have a cap on working hours, reducing strain, but states may need to hire more to maintain policing.

c2092228.titulo: Places notary offices among the functions essential to justice
c2092228.oQueMuda: Notaries and registrars would get their own section in the Constitution.
c2092228.porQueImporta: It would give notary offices a status similar to lawyers and public defenders in the Constitution, strengthening their position but also making it harder to change the rules of this service, which is profitable for its holders today.

s5073365.porQueImporta: Sport would have guaranteed funding, but this money would come from sources that today fund other areas.

s7975882.titulo: Extends book tax exemption to digital formats
s7975882.oQueMuda: Books, newspapers and magazines, including digital ones, would be free from all taxes.
s7975882.porQueImporta: Digital books and newspapers would be tax-free like printed ones, likely avoiding price increases and helping access to reading, with a small revenue loss; the Supreme Court already extended the immunity to e-books in 2017.

s7986137.titulo: Adds internet access to the fundamental and social rights
s7986137.oQueMuda: States that the State must guarantee internet access to all residents, adds internet access to the social rights and tells a law to guarantee net neutrality and quality. On its own, it does not create programs or funding: a law is needed.
s7986137.quemAfeta: People without internet access, telecom companies and governments.
s7986137.porQueImporta: The Brazilian Internet Bill of Rights already treats access as essential; the change raises it to a right in the Constitution.

s7987247.titulo: Repeals the spending cap and creates spending targets
s7987247.oQueMuda: Repeals the spending cap amendment and sets spending targets in the multi-year plan, with extra spending in 2021 and 2022.
s7987247.quemAfeta: The federal government and social program recipients.
s7987247.porQueImporta: It would end the 2016 spending cap, allowing more social spending during the pandemic but without a clear replacement rule to control debt; the cap was eventually replaced in 2023.
s7987247.apelido: End of the Spending Cap PEC

s8448291.titulo: Creates an income-based contribution to repay student loans
s8448291.oQueMuda: Allows a tax so former students repay their loans according to future income.
s8448291.quemAfeta: Students who use loans such as Fies.
s8448291.porQueImporta: Former students would repay loans according to their earnings, likely reducing defaults and risk for low earners, but creating a new tax tied to future income.

c323818.titulo: Splits oil and mining royalties by population and HDI
c323818.oQueMuda: Money from oil, gas and mining would be divided among states and cities by population, area and Human Development Index.
c323818.quemAfeta: States and cities, producers or not.
c323818.porQueImporta: States and cities that do not produce oil would receive more royalties, and producers such as Rio de Janeiro and Espírito Santo would lose revenue.

c1049154.titulo: Adds access to energy to the social rights
c1049154.oQueMuda: Adds 'access to energy' to the list of social rights. On its own, it does not create programs, funding or penalties.
c1049154.quemAfeta: People without electricity, low-income consumers and governments.
c1049154.porQueImporta: It would give a constitutional basis to policies such as social electricity rates and bringing power to those without it.

c1230264.titulo: Increases the share of income tax and IPI sent to cities
c1230264.oQueMuda: Raises the percentage of these taxes going to the Municipal Participation Fund.
c1230264.porQueImporta: City governments would receive more money, and the federal government would keep less for its own spending.

c2075915.titulo: Adds internet access to the fundamental rights
c2075915.oQueMuda: Adds to the list of fundamental rights: 'universal internet access is guaranteed to everyone'. On its own, it does not create programs, funding or penalties.
c2075915.quemAfeta: People without internet access and governments.
c2075915.porQueImporta: The Brazilian Internet Bill of Rights already treats access as essential; the change raises it to a fundamental right.

c2088568.titulo: Adds support for women victims of violence to social assistance
c2088568.oQueMuda: Social assistance would aim to support women who are victims of violence.
c2088568.porQueImporta: Women victims of violence would become a priority group for social assistance, giving a basis for demanding shelters and support, but without dedicated funding.

c2198865.titulo: Updates the wording to 'person with a disability'
c2198865.oQueMuda: The Constitution would use the phrase 'person with a disability' throughout.
c2198865.porQueImporta: It only changes the Constitution's wording, with no effect on rights; the term 'person with disability' is already used in laws and in the UN convention.

s7834640.titulo: Restricts appeals to the Supreme Court in criminal cases
s7834640.oQueMuda: Extraordinary appeals to the Supreme Court would no longer be allowed in criminal matters.
s7834640.quemAfeta: Criminal defendants and the Supreme Court.
s7834640.porQueImporta: Criminal cases would end faster, without the final stage at the Supreme Court, but defendants would lose the chance to correct violations of constitutional rights there.

s7933328.oQueMuda: The government would have to encourage payments to those who preserve nature and create jobs in environmental activities.
s7933328.porQueImporta: Those who preserve forests and rivers could be paid for it, creating income for farmers and communities, but requiring public or private money for the payments.

s7959745.titulo: Requires a list of three to choose the Prosecutor General
s7959745.oQueMuda: The President would choose the Prosecutor General from a list drawn up by federal prosecutors.
s7959745.porQueImporta: The Prosecutor General would come from a list chosen by prosecutors, giving prosecutors more independence but reducing the elected president's power and possibly strengthening internal factions.

s8323670.titulo: Gives the Supreme Court jurisdiction over crimes against democracy
s8323670.oQueMuda: Crimes against the democratic rule of law would be tried directly by the Supreme Court.
s8323670.quemAfeta: People accused of these crimes and the Supreme Court.
s8323670.porQueImporta: Attacks on democracy would be tried directly by the Supreme Court, likely speeding up cases but removing defendants' chance to appeal to other courts.

s7899802.titulo: Creates a fund to fight child poverty
s7899802.oQueMuda: Creates a fund with child poverty reduction targets and rewards for governments that make progress.
s7899802.porQueImporta: There would be targets and money to reduce child poverty, with rewards for governments that make progress, creating an incentive but also a new expense.

s7901820.titulo: Creates guarantee funds for small businesses
s7901820.oQueMuda: Creates funds to guarantee loans to micro, small and medium-sized businesses in the regions.
s7901820.porQueImporta: Small businesses would get credit more easily, because the fund covers part of the risk, which costs public money if loans are not repaid.

s7905790.titulo: Exempts donations to NGOs and research institutes from tax
s7905790.oQueMuda: Donations and bequests to nonprofit organizations would not pay the inheritance and gift tax (ITCMD).
s7905790.porQueImporta: Donations to non-profits and research would be tax-free, likely encouraging giving but reducing states' revenue from the inheritance and gift tax.

s7916284.titulo: Postponed the 2020 municipal elections because of the pandemic
s7916284.oQueMuda: Allowed the Superior Electoral Court to postpone the 2020 elections and set terms to unify elections from 2026.
s7916284.porQueImporta: Already in force (Amendment 107): it postponed the 2020 municipal elections to November because of the pandemic.

s7917387.titulo: Unifies elections by extending municipal terms
s7917387.oQueMuda: Mayors and council members elected in 2016 would serve 6-year terms to coincide with other elections.
s7917387.porQueImporta: Mayors and councilors would stay longer in office without a new election, unifying the calendar and cutting costs but extending terms beyond what voters chose.

s7917934.titulo: Counts pandemic work time double for retirement
s7917934.oQueMuda: Public health and security workers who fought COVID-19 would have that time counted double for retirement.
s7917934.porQueImporta: Professionals who worked during the pandemic would retire earlier, recognizing the risk they faced but increasing public pension spending.

c104989.titulo: Lets seconded civil servants transfer permanently
c104989.oQueMuda: Civil servants on loan to another body could choose to stay where they work.
c104989.quemAfeta: Civil servants on loan to other bodies.
c104989.porQueImporta: Seconded civil servants could stay permanently in another body, making use of people already working there but bypassing the rule of a public exam for each post.

s8077867.titulo: Extends pension debt installment plans to 240 months
s8077867.oQueMuda: Governments could pay debts to their employees' pension systems in up to 240 installments during the pandemic.
s8077867.quemAfeta: States, cities and their civil servants.
s8077867.porQueImporta: Governments would have 20 years to pay debts to civil servants' pension funds, easing finances but delaying the balance of these funds and the risk of lacking money for pensions.

s8078289.titulo: Bans tax increases during the pandemic
s8078289.oQueMuda: Governments could not create or raise taxes during the emergency, except to fight it.
s8078289.porQueImporta: Taxpayers would be protected from new taxes during disasters, but governments would have fewer options to fund the crisis response.

s8097900.titulo: Extends pension debt installment plans until 2021
s8097900.oQueMuda: Extends installment plans for governments' pension debts to 240 months and allows debt forgiveness.
s8097900.quemAfeta: States, cities and their civil servants.
s8097900.porQueImporta: Governments would get more time and partial forgiveness of pension debts, easing finances but reducing money to pay civil servants' pensions.

s8099954.titulo: Creates quotas for Black candidates and by gender in the legislature
s8099954.oQueMuda: Sets minimum shares of candidates of each gender and of Black people, and reserves campaign funds and TV time for them.
s8099954.quemAfeta: Parties, women candidates and Black candidates.
s8099954.porQueImporta: More women and Black candidates would run with resources, which tends to increase their presence in legislatures; parties would have less freedom to choose candidates and distribute money.

s8113511.titulo: Creates the Opportunities Amendment with a minimum income
s8113511.oQueMuda: Guarantees a minimum income and reserves budget money to expand early education and other opportunities.
s8113511.porQueImporta: Poor families would have guaranteed minimum income and more early-education places, likely reducing poverty but creating permanent budget expenses.

s8138727.titulo: Sends the top three candidates to the runoff
s8138727.oQueMuda: If no one wins a majority in the first round, the three top candidates would compete in the second.
s8138727.quemAfeta: Voters and candidates for president, governor and mayor.
s8138727.porQueImporta: With three candidates in the runoff, voters would have more options, but the winner could be elected without an absolute majority.

s8154053.titulo: Changes the ICMS on fuel, gas and electricity
s8154053.oQueMuda: Changes how the ICMS is charged on petroleum products, cooking gas and electricity.
s8154053.porQueImporta: Changing ICMS on fuel and energy could lower consumer prices but reduces states' main revenue, which funds health, education and security.

s8154081.titulo: Bans using the science fund to pay debt
s8154081.oQueMuda: Money from the National Science and Technology Development Fund could not be used to pay down the public debt.
s8154081.porQueImporta: Science money could not go to pay debt, protecting research but removing a source the government uses to reduce public debt.

s8158286.titulo: Creates a national career for public health system doctors
s8158286.oQueMuda: Creates a national career for doctors in the public health system (SUS), with set requirements and pay.
s8158286.quemAfeta: Doctors and patients of the SUS.
s8158286.porQueImporta: A national career could bring doctors to towns that cannot hire them today, but would be costly for the federal government and change who hires doctors, today mostly city governments.

s8163561.titulo: Creates Auxílio Brasil and transparency rules for amendments
s8163561.oQueMuda: Replaces Bolsa Família with Auxílio Brasil and requires transparency in carrying out legislators' amendments.
s8163561.porQueImporta: It dealt with replacing Bolsa Família with Auxílio Brasil in 2021, affecting millions of families and the size of social spending outside the spending cap.

s8166899.titulo: Makes basic income a social right
s8166899.oQueMuda: Guarantees income to vulnerable families and creates fiscal exceptions to pay for the benefit.
s8166899.porQueImporta: Vulnerable families would have income guaranteed in the Constitution, likely reducing poverty, and the benefit would be paid through exceptions to fiscal rules, increasing public debt.

s8167542.titulo: Sends part of legislators' amendments to fighting poverty
s8167542.oQueMuda: Part of individual budget amendments would have to go to anti-poverty actions.
s8167542.porQueImporta: Part of budget amendments would have to go to fighting poverty, directing resources to the poorest but reducing lawmakers' freedom to choose where to spend.

s7752094.titulo: Applies the salary cap to organizations receiving public money
s7752094.oQueMuda: Nonprofits funded with public resources, such as the 'S System' training bodies, would have to respect the salary cap.
s7752094.quemAfeta: Directors and staff of these organizations.
s7752094.porQueImporta: Heads of bodies such as the 'Sistema S' would have salaries capped, reducing spending of indirect public money but possibly making it harder to hire managers.

s8436103.titulo: Expands the Federal Public Defender's budget
s8436103.oQueMuda: The Federal Public Defender's Office would get yearly increases in its spending limit for 10 years.
s8436103.quemAfeta: People who rely on public defenders, and the defenders.
s8436103.porQueImporta: The Federal Public Defender's Office could grow and reach more cities, widening poor people's access to justice but increasing federal spending.

s8436730.oQueMuda: Medicines for human use would be tax-free.
s8436730.porQueImporta: Medicines would become cheaper for patients and the public health system, but the revenue loss would be large and would have to be offset by other taxes.

s8437557.titulo: Adds a Federal District appeals judge to the CNJ
s8437557.oQueMuda: The National Council of Justice would gain an appeals judge from the Federal District Court of Justice.
s8437557.quemAfeta: The Federal District courts and the CNJ.
s8437557.porQueImporta: The Federal District courts would gain a voice in the body that oversees the judiciary, changing the balance of who decides punishments and rules for judges.

c2084043.titulo: Makes spending on agricultural research mandatory
c2084043.oQueMuda: The government would have to carry out budget funds for scientific research in agriculture and livestock.
c2084043.porQueImporta: Agricultural research, such as Embrapa's, would be protected from cuts, giving studies continuity but forcing the government to cut more elsewhere when money is short.

s8305239.titulo: Gives special retirement to municipal guards
s8305239.oQueMuda: Municipal guards would be entitled to special retirement.
s8305239.porQueImporta: Municipal guards would retire earlier, recognizing the risks of the job but increasing city pension deficits.

s8306962.titulo: Raises the March FPM transfer by 1%
s8306962.oQueMuda: The federal government would hand an extra 1% of its revenue to the Municipal Participation Fund every March.
s8306962.porQueImporta: City governments would receive more money, and the federal government would keep less for its own spending.

s8319791.oQueMuda: Creates a basic income benefit with defined funding sources.
s8319791.porQueImporta: Low-income families would have a guaranteed basic income, likely reducing poverty but creating a permanent expense that depends on the planned funding sources.

s8320782.titulo: Bans selling state-owned companies between election and inauguration
s8320782.oQueMuda: Governments could not sell public assets or control of state companies during the transition period.
s8320782.porQueImporta: Governments that lost the election could not sell state companies before the successor takes office, preventing last-minute decisions but possibly delaying deals already underway.

s8329085.titulo: Bans political statements by Supreme Court justices
s8329085.oQueMuda: Justices of the Supreme Court and higher courts could not make political statements, or they would commit an impeachable offense.
s8329085.porQueImporta: Supreme Court justices who spoke about politics could be impeached, reinforcing neutrality, but 'political statement' is a broad concept that could be used to pressure the court.

s8331055.titulo: Creates an integrity system and anti-corruption courts
s8331055.oQueMuda: Establishes an integrity system in the judiciary and specialized courts for crimes against public administration.
s8331055.quemAfeta: Courts and defendants in corruption cases.
s8331055.porQueImporta: Specialized courts could speed up corruption cases, but require new judges and structures, at a cost to the judiciary.

s8332695.titulo: Gives Congress the say on suspending legislators' social media
s8332695.oQueMuda: Only the Chamber and the Senate could suspend or remove their members' online profiles and channels.
s8332695.porQueImporta: Only Congress itself could take down lawmakers' profiles, protecting them from court-ordered blocks but making it harder to stop attacks, threats or disinformation they post.

s8291388.oQueMuda: The federal government would have to create an ombudsman to receive complaints and fight violence against women.
s8291388.porQueImporta: There would be a federal channel for reporting violence against women, making reporting easier but creating a new structure and expense.

s8293254.titulo: Creates binding precedents for the Superior Court of Justice
s8293254.oQueMuda: The Superior Court of Justice could issue precedents all judges would have to follow.
s8293254.quemAfeta: Judges, lawyers and parties to cases.
s8293254.porQueImporta: Rulings by the Superior Court of Justice would bind all judges, reducing different outcomes for similar cases and the number of appeals, but reducing individual judges' freedom.

c2351680.oQueMuda: Sets criteria and bans for sentence pardons granted by the President.
c2351680.porQueImporta: The president would have less freedom to pardon sentences, preventing controversial pardons but reducing a tool also used to ease overcrowded prisons.

s7741352.titulo: Raises the share of income tax and IPI sent to states to 26%
s7741352.oQueMuda: The share of income tax and IPI for the State Participation Fund would rise by 4.5 points.
s7741352.quemAfeta: State governments and the federal government.
s7741352.porQueImporta: States would receive more money, and the federal government would keep less for its own spending.

s8402530.titulo: Adds the Federal Waterway Police to public safety
s8402530.oQueMuda: The Federal Waterway Police would become part of the public safety system.
s8402530.quemAfeta: Residents of river regions and the Federal Police.
s8402530.porQueImporta: A dedicated river police would strengthen policing in regions such as the Amazon, but creates another federal body and more staff costs.

s8406896.titulo: Adds protection of security and health workers to the fundamental rights
s8406896.oQueMuda: States that protection of public security and health workers is guaranteed, as set by law. On its own, it does not say what that protection would be: a law is needed.
s8406896.quemAfeta: Police officers, firefighters, health workers and the government.
s8406896.porQueImporta: It would give these workers a right written in the Constitution to demand protection.

s8407865.titulo: Restricts appointments to state company boards
s8407865.oQueMuda: Bans appointing people with conflicts of interest to boards and management of state-owned companies.
s8407865.porQueImporta: State companies would have fewer political appointees on their boards, which could improve management but reduces the elected government's control over these companies.

c2231670.titulo: Creates committees to reduce health lawsuits
c2231670.oQueMuda: States would have multi-agency committees to resolve health requests without going to court.
c2231670.quemAfeta: Patients, the public health system (SUS) and the judiciary.
c2231670.porQueImporta: Requests for medicines and treatments could be resolved without a lawsuit, faster for patients and easing the courts, but creating a new structure in each state.

s8220747.titulo: Lets all judges vote to elect court leadership
s8220747.oQueMuda: Court leadership (except the internal affairs office) would be elected by all tenured first- and second-instance judges in the region, by secret ballot, for 2-year terms.
s8220747.porQueImporta: All judges would vote for court leadership, broadening participation but possibly making the judiciary's internal elections more political.

s8221418.titulo: Allows converting hazardous work time to regular time for retirement
s8221418.oQueMuda: Social security contributors who worked in hazardous activities could convert that time into regular time.
s8221418.porQueImporta: Workers exposed to health risks could retire earlier, recognizing the strain but increasing INSS spending and undoing part of the 2019 reform.

s8222502.titulo: Reserves women-only lists for court seats
s8222502.oQueMuda: One in every two nomination lists for the 'constitutional fifth' seats would be made up only of women.
s8222502.quemAfeta: Women lawyers, prosecutors and the courts.
s8222502.porQueImporta: More women lawyers and prosecutors would reach the courts, where they are a minority today; male candidates would have fewer places on this path.

s8230006.oQueMuda: Donations of goods and services for humanitarian aid would be tax-free.
s8230006.porQueImporta: Donations during crises would be tax-free, likely encouraging humanitarian aid, with a small loss of revenue.

s8394951.titulo: Alternates where provisional measures start between Chamber and Senate
s8394951.oQueMuda: Provisional measures would start alternately in the Chamber and the Senate, and joint committees would be abolished.
s8394951.porQueImporta: It would change which house first reviews provisional measures, giving the Senate more power and reducing the Chamber's over these rules.

c2132847.titulo: Sends work-related social security cases to the Labor Courts
c2132847.oQueMuda: Cases about work-related social security benefits, such as accidents, would go to the Labor Courts.
c2132847.quemAfeta: Injured workers and the national social security institute (INSS).
c2132847.porQueImporta: Workplace accident claims would go to judges specialized in labor relations, which could speed up and improve these cases but shifts a power that today belongs to federal and state courts.

s7760703.titulo: Bans pardons for heinous and corruption crimes
s7760703.oQueMuda: The President could not pardon sentences for heinous crimes, money laundering and crimes against public administration.
s7760703.porQueImporta: People convicted of heinous crimes and corruption could not be pardoned by the president, preventing controversial pardons but reducing a tool also used to ease prisons.

s8373076.titulo: Strengthens protection of final court rulings
s8373076.oQueMuda: Reaffirms that final rulings cannot be undone, including by changes in Supreme Court interpretation.
s8373076.quemAfeta: Taxpayers and parties to closed cases.
s8373076.porQueImporta: Companies and people with closed cases could not be charged again because of a change in the Supreme Court's view, giving legal certainty but possibly reducing tax revenue.

c2222337.titulo: Shares pre-salt auction revenue with states and cities
c2222337.oQueMuda: The federal government would share with states and cities revenue from the pre-salt oil rights auction.
c2222337.quemAfeta: States, cities and the federal government.
c2222337.porQueImporta: Already in force (Amendment 102): states and municipalities received part of the billions from the 2019 pre-salt oil auction, and the federal government kept less.

c2351620.titulo: Requires Congress's approval for loans to other countries
c2351620.oQueMuda: Federal public banks could only lend to foreign countries with Congress's authorization.
c2351620.quemAfeta: The BNDES and other public banks.
c2351620.porQueImporta: Loans from public banks to other countries would depend on Congress, increasing control but possibly delaying Brazilian companies' business abroad.

s1400311.titulo: Sets deadlines to appoint officials approved by the Senate
s1400311.oQueMuda: Creates deadlines to choose and appoint officials such as agency directors, with an impeachable offense if missed.
s1400311.porQueImporta: Posts at agencies and other bodies would be filled faster, possibly avoiding paralysis but reducing the president's freedom of choice.

s1401169.titulo: Requires a complementary law for concession rules
s1401169.oQueMuda: Public service concessions and permits would be regulated by a complementary law.
s1401169.quemAfeta: Concession holders and public service users.
s1401169.porQueImporta: Concession rules would become more stable, possibly attracting investors, but harder to change when services are poor for users.

s3037753.titulo: Changes how the Cide fuel tax is shared with states and cities
s3037753.oQueMuda: Redistributes the revenue from the Cide fuel tax differently among states and cities.
s3037753.porQueImporta: It would change how much each state and municipality receives from the fuel levy, used for roads and transport.

s7411048.titulo: Makes it easier to arrest and prosecute legislators
s7411048.oQueMuda: Allows arresting legislators after a second-instance conviction and ends Congress's power to block arrests and cases.
s7411048.porQueImporta: Lawmakers could be arrested and prosecuted without their colleagues' approval, making it easier to punish politicians' crimes but reducing a protection against political persecution.

s1401465.oQueMuda: Changes the system of government to parliamentarism, with a prime minister.
s1401465.porQueImporta: The government would depend on congressional support and could fall without an election, making it easier to replace unpopular governments but possibly creating more instability; in 1993 the country chose presidentialism in a referendum.

s1401414.titulo: Changes how attorneys general are chosen
s1401414.oQueMuda: The Prosecutor General could also come from state prosecutors' offices, and attorneys general would have to step down before seeking reappointment.
s1401414.porQueImporta: It would change who can head the prosecution service and make it harder for a prosecutor general to use the post to be reappointed, affecting independence and the president's influence.

s7914500.titulo: Creates a fixed term and list of three for the Federal Police chief
s7914500.oQueMuda: The Federal Police director would be chosen from a list of three, with a three-year term and Senate approval.
s7914500.quemAfeta: The Federal Police and the Presidency.
s7914500.porQueImporta: The head of the Federal Police would have a fixed term and come from a list, giving investigations more independence but reducing the elected government's control over an armed police force.

s7989488.titulo: Requires officeholders to step down to seek reelection
s7989488.oQueMuda: The President, governors and mayors seeking reelection would have to take leave six months before.
s7989488.quemAfeta: Heads of the executive and voters.
s7989488.porQueImporta: Leaders would have to leave office to seek re-election, reducing the use of government resources in campaigns but leaving the deputy in charge for six months.

c2325720.titulo: Halves city governments' social security contributions
c2325720.oQueMuda: Cities would pay half the contribution rate on their payroll.
c2325720.porQueImporta: City governments would pay half the social security contribution and have more money, but INSS would lose billions in revenue, increasing its deficit.

c501028.titulo: Allows using court-ordered government debts to buy a home
c501028.oQueMuda: Credits from court-ordered government debts (precatórios) could be used to buy a home.
c501028.porQueImporta: People owed court-ordered payments could use them to buy a home, giving immediate use to credit that takes years to be paid; the cost would fall on banks or governments accepting these credits.

s1401223.titulo: Guarantees women seats on Congress's governing boards and committees
s1401223.oQueMuda: The makeup of governing boards and committees would have to be proportional to the number of each gender.
s1401223.porQueImporta: Women would have guaranteed places in the leadership of Congress and committees, where they are a minority today; parties would have less freedom to appoint their members.

s8392917.titulo: Changes where the President's bills start
s8392917.oQueMuda: Bills from the President and the courts could start in the Senate, not only in the Chamber.
s8392917.porQueImporta: Government bills could start in the Senate, giving the Senate more power and reducing the Chamber's, which today has the first say.

s8133142.titulo: Requires free, science-based public health care
s8133142.oQueMuda: Public health actions and services would have to be free and based on scientific evidence.
s8133142.quemAfeta: Patients of the public health system (SUS).
s8133142.porQueImporta: Requiring a scientific basis could keep treatments without proven efficacy out of the public health system, but also makes it harder to offer new or alternative therapies.

s8171441.titulo: Sets rules for adding new treatments to the public health system
s8171441.oQueMuda: Creates criteria for adding new medicines and procedures to the SUS, with mandatory prior review.
s8171441.porQueImporta: Rules for adding treatments to the public health system could bring criteria and spending control, but also delay access to new drugs, which many patients today obtain through the courts.

s1394077.titulo: Reserves legislative seats for people with disabilities
s1394077.oQueMuda: Seats in the Chamber, state assemblies and city councils would be reserved for people with disabilities for four legislatures.
s1394077.porQueImporta: People with disabilities would have guaranteed seats in legislatures, increasing their representation but limiting voters' choice for those seats.

s1394130.titulo: Creates the Racial Equality Promotion Fund
s1394130.oQueMuda: Creates a fund for policies including Black Brazilians in housing, education and job training.
s1394130.porQueImporta: Policies for Black Brazilians would have fixed federal tax money, protected from cuts, reducing the share passed on to other areas.

s1394231.titulo: Gives priority to bills on the same subject as provisional measures
s1394231.oQueMuda: Bills on the same topic as a provisional measure would be reviewed alongside it, with priority for the oldest.
s1394231.porQueImporta: Lawmakers' bills would gain weight against the government's provisional measures, strengthening Congress but possibly slowing down review of those measures.

s1394282.titulo: Creates national rules for public service exams
s1394282.oQueMuda: Exams would have to offer all open positions, and exams just for a waiting list or new exams with approved candidates still waiting would be banned.
s1394282.porQueImporta: People who pass public exams would have more assurance of being called, protecting candidates but reducing agencies' flexibility to hire according to their budget.

s1394688.titulo: Extends special retirement rules for teachers in the transition
s1394688.oQueMuda: Basic education teachers would get five years off the requirements under the 2005 transition rule too.
s1394688.porQueImporta: More teachers would retire earlier, correcting a transition rule but increasing pension spending by states and municipalities.

s1394843.titulo: Adjusts pensions by the most favorable inflation index
s1394843.oQueMuda: Social security benefits would be adjusted by the inflation index most favorable to retirees.
s1394843.quemAfeta: Retirees and pensioners of the national social security system.
s1394843.porQueImporta: Retirees would always get the highest adjustment among several indexes, protecting their income but increasing social security spending, the largest federal expense.

s1394997.titulo: Calls an assembly to carry out political reform
s1394997.oQueMuda: Voters would elect representatives to a review assembly devoted only to political and electoral reform.
s1394997.porQueImporta: An assembly elected only for political reform could change rules Congress avoids touching, but also opens room for broad changes outside the normal limits on amendments.

s1402212.oQueMuda: People not affiliated with parties could run in elections.
s1402212.porQueImporta: People outside parties could run for office, widening voters' choices but possibly fragmenting Congress further and weakening parties.

s7242157.titulo: Automatically removes legislators convicted under the Clean Record Law
s7242157.oQueMuda: Deputies and senators convicted of crimes that cause ineligibility would lose their seats automatically.
s7242157.porQueImporta: Convicted lawmakers would lose their seats without a vote by colleagues, preventing the house from protecting its members but taking away a decision Congress makes about itself.

s7399577.titulo: Reserves 2% of legislators' amendments for sports
s7399577.oQueMuda: At least 2% of individual budget amendments would go to sports.
s7399577.porQueImporta: Sport would have guaranteed funding through budget amendments, but less amendment money would be left for other areas, such as health and public works.

c1280152.titulo: Charges ICMS on interstate electricity sales
c1280152.oQueMuda: The ICMS would apply to electricity transactions between states.
c1280152.porQueImporta: Energy-producing states, such as those with large hydropower plants, would collect more, and electricity bills in other states could rise.

c1594140.titulo: Allows reducing states' delegations in the Chamber
c1594140.oQueMuda: Ends the rule that prevents reducing the number of deputies from each state.
c1594140.porQueImporta: States that lost population could lose deputies and growing ones would gain, making each vote's weight more equal but reducing smaller states' representation.

c609753.titulo: Federal aid to pay the nursing salary floor
c609753.oQueMuda: The federal government would give financial support to states, municipalities, charities and private providers serving at least 60% public health system (SUS) patients so they can pay the nursing salary floor.
c609753.quemAfeta: Nursing professionals, city governments, charity hospitals and hospitals serving SUS.
c609753.porQueImporta: Already in force: the federal government began helping pay the nursing salary floor, making the raise possible at a cost of billions a year to the federal budget.

c1701050.titulo: Bans creating costs for governments without naming a funding source
c1701050.oQueMuda: Laws could not impose costs on federal, state and city governments without provision in the budget.
c1701050.porQueImporta: Congress could not create costs for states and cities without saying who pays, protecting local finances but possibly making it harder to pass laws that expand rights.

c43596.titulo: Guarantees yearly funding for the Amazon and Northeast funds
c43596.oQueMuda: A law would set mandatory yearly amounts for these regions' development funds.
c43596.quemAfeta: Companies and governments in the Amazon and Northeast.
c43596.porQueImporta: The Amazon and Northeast would have guaranteed development money, reducing room in the federal budget for other areas.

c2194899.titulo: Takes federal university spending out of the cap (text of the Transition PEC)
c2194899.oQueMuda: Excludes federal education institutions' spending from the spending cap; in 2022 it was the text used to vote on the Transition PEC.
c2194899.porQueImporta: Already in force (Amendment 126): it was the text used for the 2022 Transition PEC, which allowed spending outside the cap in 2023, such as the R$600 Bolsa Família, at the cost of more spending and debt.

c620527.oQueMuda: Federal and state governments would have to spend a minimum percentage on cultural heritage and cultural production.
c620527.porQueImporta: Culture would have mandatory minimum spending, like health and education, guaranteeing funding but reducing room for other budget areas.

c2095531.titulo: Adds reciprocity to the principles of foreign policy
c2095531.oQueMuda: Adds 'reciprocity' (treating other countries as they treat Brazil) to the list of principles of international relations. On its own, it does not create programs, funding or penalties.
c2095531.quemAfeta: The federal government, diplomacy and Brazilians abroad.
c2095531.porQueImporta: It would guide foreign policy decisions, such as visa and trade rules.

c2194813.oQueMuda: Cooking gas for household use would be tax-free.
c2194813.porQueImporta: Cooking gas could become cheaper for families, especially the poorest, but states and the federal government would lose revenue.

c2230007.titulo: Guarantees income for families in poverty
c2230007.oQueMuda: Social assistance would have to guarantee cash transfers to poor and extremely poor families.
c2230007.porQueImporta: A cash-transfer program would be guaranteed in the Constitution, protected from changes in government, creating a permanent item in the budget.

c2285501.titulo: Let cities pay pension debts in 240 installments
c2285501.oQueMuda: In 2021, cities could pay their social security debts in up to 240 monthly installments.
c2285501.porQueImporta: Already in force since 2021: city governments got 20 years to pay pension debts, easing finances but delaying money owed to INSS and civil servants' funds.

c2304959.titulo: Puts climate security into the Constitution
c2304959.oQueMuda: Adds 'climate security' to the fundamental rights and to the principles of the economy, and tells the government to act against climate change and its effects. It does not say which actions nor create funding.
c2304959.quemAfeta: The whole population, companies and governments.
c2304959.porQueImporta: The Constitution already guarantees a balanced environment; the change mentions climate explicitly, which can be used in laws and in court.

c2336964.titulo: Federal aid to pay the nursing minimum wage
c2336964.oQueMuda: The federal government would give financial support to states, cities and charities to meet the nursing minimum salary.
c2336964.porQueImporta: The federal government would help pay the nursing salary floor, making the raise possible at a cost of billions a year to the federal budget.

s7728717.titulo: Adds the National Force to the public safety bodies
s7728717.oQueMuda: The National Public Safety Force would be a permanent body for cooperation among governments.
s7728717.quemAfeta: The National Force and the states.
s7728717.porQueImporta: The National Force would have a constitutional basis, giving stability to federal support for states but possibly reducing states' autonomy over security in their territory.

s7732135.titulo: Separates electoral crimes from ordinary crimes in court cases
s7732135.oQueMuda: Ordinary crimes linked to electoral crimes would be tried by the regular courts.
s7732135.quemAfeta: Defendants in corruption and slush-fund cases.
s7732135.porQueImporta: Corruption cases linked to illegal campaign funds would leave the Electoral Courts, which have less capacity to investigate complex crimes, and go to ordinary courts.

s7733509.titulo: Allows holding two public journalist jobs
s7733509.oQueMuda: Journalists could hold two public posts with compatible hours.
s7733509.porQueImporta: Journalists in public service could hold two posts and two incomes, setting a precedent for other careers and increasing staff costs.

s7738877.oQueMuda: Limits the number and duration of provisional measures, bans them on labor matters and bans unrelated add-ons.
s7738877.porQueImporta: The president would have less room to govern by provisional measures, giving Congress more power but possibly delaying quick government responses.

s7741158.titulo: Requires technical selection of federal audit court ministers
s7741158.oQueMuda: Federal audit court ministers would be chosen from auditors and prosecutors with no recent elected office.
s7741158.porQueImporta: Federal Audit Court ministers would be career auditors rather than politicians, reducing political appointments but also the influence of Congress and the president over the court.

s7745408.titulo: Ends 60-day vacations and allows judges to be dismissed
s7745408.oQueMuda: Judges and prosecutors would have 30 days of vacation, would not be punished with retirement and could be dismissed.
s7745408.porQueImporta: Judges and prosecutors would lose benefits, such as 60 days of vacation, and could lose their post as punishment, reducing spending but affecting guarantees created for the independence of these careers.

s7748831.titulo: Allows public universities to charge for services
s7748831.oQueMuda: Universities could charge for services they provide and manage their own revenue.
s7748831.porQueImporta: Universities could earn money from services and research, reducing dependence on government but possibly drawing some away from free teaching.

s7752601.titulo: Moves the rural land tax to the municipalities
s7752601.oQueMuda: Cities would collect the rural land tax (ITR), now charged by the federal government.
s7752601.porQueImporta: Rural towns would collect the rural land tax, increasing their revenue, but local collection may be more exposed to pressure from large landowners.

s7753206.titulo: Creates Supreme Court terms and selection by Congress
s7753206.oQueMuda: Some justices of the Supreme Court and higher courts would be chosen by the Chamber and the Senate, with fixed terms.
s7753206.porQueImporta: Congress would choose some Supreme Court and higher-court justices, increasing politicians' influence over those who judge them.

s7753619.titulo: Caps interest rates charged by banks
s7753619.oQueMuda: Banks could not charge more than three times the Selic benchmark rate.
s7753619.porQueImporta: Credit card and overdraft rates would fall, helping indebted people, but banks may deny credit to riskier borrowers, pushing people toward loan sharks.

s7759040.titulo: Adjusts federal transfers to cities for inflation
s7759040.oQueMuda: Balances of federal programs with cities would be updated for inflation every year.
s7759040.porQueImporta: City governments would receive inflation-adjusted amounts in federal programs, keeping transfers' purchasing power but increasing federal spending.

s7759495.titulo: Requires drug testing of police and firefighters
s7759495.oQueMuda: Public safety professionals would undergo periodic drug testing.
s7759495.porQueImporta: Police officers and firefighters would undergo periodic drug tests, which could remove drug users from armed duties, but creates costs and privacy debates.

s7774325.oQueMuda: Products made mainly from recycled material would be tax-free.
s7774325.porQueImporta: Recycled products would become cheaper, likely encouraging recycling, with a loss of revenue.

s7775664.titulo: Bans reissuing decrees struck down by Congress
s7775664.oQueMuda: The government could not reissue, in the same year, a decree halted by Congress.
s7775664.porQueImporta: The government could not reissue a decree overturned by Congress, strengthening legislative control over the executive.

s7775894.titulo: Raises the share of income tax and IPI sent to cities to 30%
s7775894.oQueMuda: An extra 5.5% of these taxes would go to the Municipal Participation Fund.
s7775894.porQueImporta: City governments would receive more money, and the federal government would keep less for its own spending.

s7786111.oQueMuda: Mayors and council members elected in 2020 would serve six years to unify elections in 2026.
s7786111.porQueImporta: Mayors and councilors elected in 2020 would serve six years, unifying the calendar and cutting costs but extending terms beyond what voters chose.

s7798303.titulo: Guarantees minimum public investment of 1.5% of GDP
s7798303.oQueMuda: The federal government would have to invest at least 1.5% of GDP, outside the spending cap.
s7798303.porQueImporta: There would be guaranteed minimum investment in public works, which could boost the economy but increases spending and public debt, since it would be outside the spending limit.

s7811689.titulo: Allows endowment funds for federal universities
s7811689.oQueMuda: Universities could create funds from donations, and donors would get tax benefits.
s7811689.porQueImporta: Universities could receive donations into their own endowments, creating extra funding; tax benefits for donors reduce revenue.

s7822485.titulo: Uses regional funds for state and city infrastructure
s7822485.oQueMuda: For five years, 30% of the North, Northeast and Center-West funds would go to infrastructure works.
s7822485.quemAfeta: States and cities in these regions.
s7822485.porQueImporta: Governments in these regions would have more money for public works, but less cheap credit would remain for local companies and producers.

s7822487.titulo: Compensates states and cities hosting rocket launch bases
s7822487.oQueMuda: Places with aerospace launch centers would receive compensation and a social fund.
s7822487.quemAfeta: Residents of Alcântara (Maranhão) and the surrounding region.
s7822487.porQueImporta: Communities affected by rocket launch bases, such as the quilombola communities of Alcântara, would receive compensation, creating a new federal expense.

s7828021.titulo: Protects pregnant civil servants in appointed posts
s7828021.oQueMuda: Women in appointed posts could not be dismissed from pregnancy until five months after birth.
s7828021.quemAfeta: Women civil servants in appointed posts.
s7828021.porQueImporta: Pregnant appointees could not be dismissed, protecting them but limiting governments' freedom to change teams.

s7845448.titulo: Creates a national fund for environmental emergencies
s7845448.oQueMuda: Creates a fund of the federal government and coastal states to prevent and repair environmental disasters.
s7845448.quemAfeta: Coastal residents and people in risk areas.
s7845448.porQueImporta: Money would be set aside to respond to coastal disasters, like the 2019 oil spill, but requires funds that today go to other areas.

s7971591.titulo: Adds fighting corruption to the foundations of the Republic
s7971591.oQueMuda: Adds 'preventing and fighting corruption' to the country's foundations, alongside sovereignty, citizenship and human dignity. On its own, it does not create programs, funding or penalties.
s7971591.quemAfeta: The whole population, public bodies and lawmakers.
s7971591.porQueImporta: The Constitution already requires integrity in public administration; the change would give the issue more weight in how laws are interpreted.

s8153922.titulo: Lets legislators become ambassadors without losing their seats
s8153922.oQueMuda: Deputies and senators could head embassies without losing their seats.
s8153922.porQueImporta: Lawmakers could become ambassadors without losing their seats, bringing diplomacy closer to party politics and letting the government offer posts in exchange for support.

s8228548.titulo: Defines what happens to public forests
s8228548.oQueMuda: Sets deadlines and rules for allocating public forest land and bans transferring it to third parties in some cases.
s8228548.quemAfeta: Forest communities, governments and land occupants.
s8228548.porQueImporta: Public forest lands would have deadlines and rules for their use, making land grabbing harder but possibly creating conflicts with current occupants.

s7749502.titulo: Gives the Federal District ownership of its constitutional fund
s7749502.oQueMuda: Money in the fund that pays for police, firefighters and services in the Federal District would belong to the district.
s7749502.quemAfeta: The government and residents of the Federal District.
s7749502.porQueImporta: The Federal District would have more autonomy over the money the federal government sends for police, health and education, reducing federal control over this spending.

s8266998.titulo: Makes Ibama and ICMBio permanent institutions
s8266998.oQueMuda: The environmental agencies Ibama and ICMBio would become permanent state institutions.
s8266998.porQueImporta: Ibama and ICMBio could not be abolished by a government, giving stability to environmental enforcement but reducing freedom to reorganize these bodies.

s8199287.titulo: Creates guarantees for police, firefighters and their families
s8199287.oQueMuda: Police and firefighters would be entitled to health care, life insurance and support for relatives.
s8199287.porQueImporta: Police, firefighters and their families would have guaranteed insurance and assistance, recognizing the job's risks and increasing state spending.

s8136536.titulo: Makes IBGE, Inep and evaluation bodies permanent institutions
s8136536.oQueMuda: Statistics and education evaluation bodies would be permanent, with rules for choosing their heads.
s8136536.porQueImporta: IBGE and Inep would be protected from abolition and interference in choosing their heads, increasing trust in official data but reducing the elected government's control.

s7969278.titulo: Defines how old Fundef court payments are used
s7969278.oQueMuda: Court-ordered payments from the old Fundef education fund would go to basic education, with part used to pay teachers.
s7969278.porQueImporta: Billions owed by the federal government to the former Fundef would go to education, with part for teachers, settling who gets this money, which governments wanted to use elsewhere.

s8104778.titulo: Changes management of the Center-West fund
s8104778.oQueMuda: Sudeco could authorize banks to manage the Center-West financing fund.
s8104778.porQueImporta: More banks could operate the Center-West fund, which could widen access to credit but changes control that is today concentrated at Banco do Brasil.

s7731793.oQueMuda: Only parties with 5% of the vote for the Chamber or 20 deputies would be represented in Congress.
s7731793.porQueImporta: Fewer parties would hold seats in Congress, which could make deals and governing easier but removes representation from voters of small parties.

s7812089.titulo: Sends half of legislators' amendments to health and education
s7812089.oQueMuda: Half of individual budget amendments would go to health and education, in equal parts.
s7812089.porQueImporta: Half of budget amendments would go to health and education, directing resources to these areas but reducing lawmakers' freedom to choose where to spend.

s7852681.titulo: Changes how presidential vetoes are voted on
s7852681.oQueMuda: Vetoes would be voted on separately in the Chamber and the Senate, except those on budget laws.
s7852681.porQueImporta: Vetoes would be voted separately by deputies and senators, changing each house's weight and making overrides slower.

s7869752.titulo: Lets Brazilians abroad vote for senator and governor
s7869752.oQueMuda: Brazilians living abroad would have special districts to vote in majority-vote elections.
