s7869752.porQueImporta: Brazilians abroad would have a say in elections for senator and governor, expanding their representation but requiring special constituencies and more election logistics.

s7740538.oQueMuda: Sets conditions and personal requirements for holding appointed posts and positions of trust.
s7740538.quemAfeta: Holders of appointed posts and governments.
s7740538.porQueImporta: Appointed posts would have minimum requirements, reducing unqualified appointments but limiting elected governments' freedom to choose their teams.

s7733785.titulo: Makes the Fundeb education fund permanent
s7733785.oQueMuda: The main fund financing basic education would no longer have an end date.
s7733785.porQueImporta: Fundeb, which pays a large share of teachers' salaries, would no longer expire; the change entered the Constitution in 2020 through another PEC (Amendment 108), with a larger federal share.

s7748936.titulo: Makes Fundeb permanent with universal access targets
s7748936.oQueMuda: Makes Fundeb permanent and requires targets to make basic education universal and expand daycare.
s7748936.porQueImporta: Fundeb, which pays a large share of teachers' salaries, would no longer expire; the change entered the Constitution in 2020 through another PEC (Amendment 108), with a larger federal share.

s7741529.titulo: Bans special pension plans for politicians
s7741529.oQueMuda: There could be no separate retirement systems for elected officials.
s7741529.porQueImporta: Politicians would have the same retirement rules as other workers, reducing spending and privileges; the 2019 pension reform already closed the old lawmakers' plan to newly elected members.

s7753204.titulo: Takes pre-salt bonus transfers out of the spending cap
s7753204.oQueMuda: Transfers to states and cities from the oil signing bonus would not count toward the spending cap.
s7753204.quemAfeta: States, cities and the federal government.
s7753204.porQueImporta: It allowed sharing billions from the pre-salt oil auction with states and cities without breaching the spending cap, increasing total government spending that year.

s8143032.titulo: Requires a woman on every executive ticket
s8143032.oQueMuda: Tickets for president and governor would have to include at least one woman.
s8143032.porQueImporta: Every executive ticket would include a woman, increasing women's presence in government but limiting parties' choices when forming tickets.

s7724131.titulo: Counts military service in police entrance exams
s7724131.oQueMuda: Mandatory military service would count as a credential or tiebreaker in exams for police, firefighters and municipal guards.
s7724131.porQueImporta: Those who served in the armed forces would have an advantage in police exams, valuing military experience but disadvantaging women, who generally do not do military service.

s7834859.titulo: Lets prosecutors receive tax data without a court order
s7834859.oQueMuda: Oversight bodies would share tax and banking data with prosecutors without a court's authorization.
s7834859.quemAfeta: People under investigation, the tax authority, the financial intelligence unit (Coaf) and prosecutors.
s7834859.porQueImporta: Money laundering and corruption investigations would be faster, but bank and tax data would be shared without a court order, reducing a privacy protection.

s7783547.oQueMuda: Bans appointing relatives to positions of trust, with penalties for misconduct.
s7783547.porQueImporta: The ban on appointing relatives, which today comes from a Supreme Court ruling, would be in the Constitution with penalties for misconduct, making loopholes and future changes harder.

s7804584.titulo: Adds conciliation and mediation to the fundamental rights
s7804584.oQueMuda: States that the State will ensure ways of settling disputes outside the courts, such as conciliation and mediation. On its own, it does not create programs, funding or penalties.
s7804584.quemAfeta: People in disputes, lawyers and the courts.
s7804584.porQueImporta: The Code of Civil Procedure already encourages these methods; the change puts them in the Constitution.

s7845422.titulo: Requires Congress's approval to clear the Amazon
s7845422.oQueMuda: Cutting vegetation in the Amazon rainforest would require prior approval from Congress.
s7845422.quemAfeta: Farmers, forest peoples and environmental agencies.
s7845422.porQueImporta: Clearing vegetation in the Amazon would depend on Congress, increasing forest protection but making public works and economic activity in the region harder, including legal ones.

s7733746.oQueMuda: Merit-based promotion of judges would consider the top half of the seniority list.
s7733746.porQueImporta: It would change who can be promoted on merit, which could favor more senior judges and reduce the influence of subjective criteria.

s7748924.titulo: Brings back coalitions in city council elections
s7748924.oQueMuda: Parties could form coalitions in municipal proportional elections.
s7748924.porQueImporta: Small parties could again form coalitions to elect councilors, giving them better chances, but a vote may help elect a candidate from another party in the coalition.

s7737914.titulo: Takes public investment out of the spending cap
s7737914.oQueMuda: Investment spending would not count toward the spending cap.
s7737914.quemAfeta: The federal government and public works sectors.
s7737914.porQueImporta: Public investment would be outside the spending limit, which could boost works and the economy but increases total spending and public debt.

s7738872.titulo: Guarantees minimum federal funding for public safety
s7738872.oQueMuda: The federal government would spend increasing amounts on the Unified Public Safety System, up to 2.5% of its revenue.
s7738872.porQueImporta: Security would have a growing minimum federal spending level, guaranteeing police funding but reducing budget room for other areas.

s7741423.titulo: Requires a list of three to choose the Prosecutor General
s7741423.oQueMuda: The Prosecutor General would be chosen from a list drawn up by members of the prosecution service.
s7741423.porQueImporta: The Prosecutor General would come from a list chosen by prosecutors, giving prosecutors more independence but reducing the elected president's power and possibly strengthening internal factions.

s7741534.oQueMuda: Repeals Amendment 95, which created the public spending cap.
s7741534.quemAfeta: The federal government and public policies.
s7741534.porQueImporta: It would end the 2016 spending cap, allowing more social spending but without a replacement rule to control debt; the cap was eventually replaced in 2023.
s7741534.apelido: End of the Spending Cap PEC

s7752275.titulo: Bans pardons for people convicted of corruption
s7752275.oQueMuda: The President could not pardon sentences for crimes against public administration, except on humanitarian grounds.
s7752275.porQueImporta: People convicted of corruption could not be pardoned by the president, except on humanitarian grounds, preventing controversial pardons and reducing presidential power.

s7717123.titulo: Ends the benefit for prisoners' families
s7717123.oQueMuda: The benefit paid to prisoners' dependents would end.
s7717123.porQueImporta: Low-income prisoners' families, usually with young children, would lose this income; social security would save on the benefit.

s7718602.titulo: Allows imprisonment after a second-instance conviction
s7718602.oQueMuda: Sentences would start after conviction by an appeals court, even with appeals pending.
s7718602.porQueImporta: People convicted by appeal courts would start serving sentences earlier, likely speeding up punishment, including of politicians, but reducing the chance to correct errors in higher courts before imprisonment.

s7876385.titulo: Bans budget freezes at federal universities
s7876385.oQueMuda: Federal universities and institutes could not have funds frozen.
s7876385.porQueImporta: Federal universities and institutes would be protected from freezes, giving stability to teaching and research but forcing the government to cut more elsewhere when money is short.

s7833783.titulo: Abolishes public funds not confirmed by law
s7833783.oQueMuda: Public funds would require a complementary law, and existing ones would be abolished if not ratified.
s7833783.quemAfeta: The government and areas financed by funds.
s7833783.porQueImporta: Funds without a law would be abolished and their idle money would go to other spending or debt, giving the government more freedom but possibly taking resources from areas such as science and the environment.

s7862583.titulo: Lets legislators use office allowance savings for social amendments
s7862583.oQueMuda: Legislators could send whatever they don't spend from their office allowance to social policies.
s7862583.porQueImporta: Lawmakers could send unspent office allowances to social policies, putting the money to use but increasing their power to direct resources to their electoral bases.

s7857865.titulo: Adds climate stability to the principles of the economy
s7857865.oQueMuda: The economic order would have to seek climate stability and the government would have to act against climate change.
s7857865.porQueImporta: It would give a constitutional basis for demanding climate policies and for interpreting economic laws; it does not create concrete obligations by itself.

s7854831.titulo: Changes the dates of executive elections
s7854831.oQueMuda: Elections for president, governor and mayor would be held in late November and early December.
s7854831.porQueImporta: Executive elections would be closer to inauguration, shortening the transition period but also the time for the new government to prepare.

s7853132.oQueMuda: Senators, deputies and council members would not be reimbursed for housing or relocation.
s7853132.porQueImporta: Lawmakers would no longer receive housing allowances, reducing legislative spending; those not living in Brasília would pay for housing from their own salary.

s7853575.titulo: Bans new pension tax breaks while the spending cap applies
s7853575.oQueMuda: The federal government could not create or expand pension exemptions and benefits while the fiscal regime is in force.
s7853575.quemAfeta: Sectors with exemptions and social security.
s7853575.porQueImporta: The federal government could not create new pension contribution exemptions, protecting its finances but preventing incentives for sectors that depend on tax relief to keep jobs.

s7849073.oQueMuda: Political parties would become public-law legal entities.
s7849073.porQueImporta: Parties would become public entities, increasing oversight of their money but reducing their freedom of internal organization.

s7717281.titulo: Lowers the age of criminal responsibility to 16
s7717281.oQueMuda: Only people under 16 would be exempt from criminal responsibility.
s7717281.quemAfeta: Teenagers aged 16 and 17 and the justice system.
s7717281.porQueImporta: More teenagers would go into the adult prison system, which is already overcrowded and where gangs recruit inmates; punishment would be harsher and prison costs would rise.

s7728643.titulo: Lowers the age of criminal responsibility to 15 for serious crimes
s7728643.oQueMuda: Young people aged 15 to 17 could be tried as adults for serious crimes, based on a judge's assessment.
s7728643.porQueImporta: Teenagers from 15 could go to adult prisons for serious crimes, toughening punishment but placing them in overcrowded prisons where gangs recruit inmates.

s7838773.titulo: Protects Suframa's own revenue from freezes
s7838773.oQueMuda: Fees and fines collected by the Manaus Free Trade Zone authority could not be frozen.
s7838773.quemAfeta: Suframa and companies in the Free Trade Zone.
s7838773.porQueImporta: Suframa's money would be protected from freezes, giving stability to Manaus Free Zone management but forcing the government to cut more elsewhere.

s7834578.titulo: Requires a plurality of ideas on radio and TV
s7834578.oQueMuda: Broadcasters would have to follow the principle of diversity of opinion in their programming.
s7834578.porQueImporta: Broadcasters would have to show a diversity of opinions, which could broaden debate but opens room for government interference in radio and TV content.

s7831603.titulo: Creates a fund against oil pollution
s7831603.oQueMuda: Creates a fund to fight and reduce damage from oil and fuel spills.
s7831603.porQueImporta: Money would be set aside to respond to oil spills, speeding up cleanup and support for fishers but requiring funds that today go to other areas.

s7812302.titulo: Bans perks for former elected officials
s7812302.oQueMuda: Former presidents, governors and legislators would get no pensions, cars, security or staff paid by the state.
s7812302.porQueImporta: Former presidents, governors and lawmakers would lose pensions and services paid by the State, reducing spending; former presidents would also lose government-paid security.

s7812304.titulo: Bans provisional measures on labor and pensions that cut rights
s7812304.oQueMuda: Provisional measures on labor and pensions would only be allowed to expand benefits.
s7812304.porQueImporta: Labor and pension rights could only be reduced by a law passed by Congress, giving more security but taking away a fast way for the government to act in crises.

s7801877.oQueMuda: Officials could give up their special court privilege and be tried in lower courts.
s7801877.porQueImporta: Officials could choose to be tried at first instance, which could be used to pick the slowest or most favorable route for the defendant.

s7797419.titulo: Uses privatization money for pensions and debt
s7797419.oQueMuda: Money from selling federal property and state companies would go to social security and paying the public debt.
s7797419.porQueImporta: Privatization money would go to pensions and debt, helping long-term finances but preventing its use for investment or social programs.

s7788918.titulo: Bans taxes on the basic food basket
s7788918.oQueMuda: Federal, state and city governments could not tax products in the basic food basket.
s7788918.porQueImporta: Basic food basket items would be tax-free, which could make food cheaper, especially for the poorest; the 2023 tax reform already zeroed taxes on a national basic food basket.

s7788352.titulo: Bans forced retirement as a punishment for judges
s7788352.oQueMuda: Judges could no longer be punished with retirement in the public interest.
s7788352.porQueImporta: Punished judges would no longer retire with pay; punishment would be harsher and public coffers would stop paying these benefits.

s7711916.titulo: Requires open votes to elect Congress's leadership
s7711916.oQueMuda: The speakers of the Chamber and the Senate would be chosen by open vote.
s7711916.porQueImporta: Voters would know whom each lawmaker voted for as head of the Chamber and Senate, increasing transparency but exposing lawmakers to pressure from the government and candidates.

s7726829.titulo: Punishes trading posts for political advantage
s7726829.oQueMuda: Appointing or dismissing people to gain political advantage or influence another branch would be misconduct.
s7726829.porQueImporta: Trading posts for political support would become misconduct, which could curb such deals, but the line between political coalition-building and trading favors is hard to prove.

s7756801.titulo: Takes health out of the spending cap
s7756801.oQueMuda: The health minimum would be adjusted above inflation and kept outside the spending cap.
s7756801.quemAfeta: Patients of the public health system (SUS) and the government.
s7756801.porQueImporta: Health would have more guaranteed money outside the spending limit, helping the public health system but increasing total spending and public debt.

s7746248.oQueMuda: Federal, state and city governments would create funds for infrastructure in metropolitan regions.
s7746248.porQueImporta: Large cities would have funds for metropolitan transport and works, helping regional planning but requiring money from all three levels of government.

s7730777.titulo: Changes how ICMS is split among cities
s7730777.oQueMuda: Lowers from 75% to 50% the share of ICMS split according to each city's economic activity.
s7730777.porQueImporta: Towns with little industry and commerce would receive more ICMS, and richer cities, home to factories and companies, would lose revenue.
